# Screen use to end in ECE and limits set in primary

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/news/260920-screen-use-to-end-in-ece-and-limits-set> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## Screen use to end in ECE and limits set in primary

20 September 2026

·

Erica Stanford

National will introduce new initiatives to ensure kids are ready for school, including an end to screens in early childhood education centres, setting limits in primary school and a new School Start Check to help kids transition from ECE to school.

National’s Education spokesperson Erica Stanford says these changes will form part of National’s Set Up for Success policy, focused on school readiness, better information for parents, and earlier support where needed.

“Young children are spending increasingly longer on screens, at the same time as the evidence tells us we should be cautious about excessive use.

“For younger children, we want to place greater emphasis on books, handwriting, conversation, hands-on activities and direct interaction with teachers and other children.

“In ECE, that means ending screen and individual-device use. In Years 1 to 3, screen use will be tightly limited, with age-appropriate limits also introduced for older primary students.

“Technology still has a place in education, but it should enhance learning, not become the default way children learn.

“That is why we are introducing Set up for Success, a series of steps that will ensure your child is school ready,” Ms Stanford says.

A re-elected National Government will:

- end screen and individual-device use in ECE, tightly limit screen and individual-device use in Years 1 to 3, and introduce age-appropriate limits for older primary students

- introduce a School Start Check at ECE before children transition to primary school

- introduce clearer developmental milestones throughout ECE and report this progress to parents

- identify areas where children may need additional support and address that through the Early Intervention Service

- require the writing component of twice-yearly primary school assessments to be completed on paper.

Ms Stanford says New Zealand is not alone in reconsidering how much time young children should spend learning through screens.

“The direction internationally is increasingly clear. Particularly for young children, digital does not automatically mean better.

“There is also growing evidence about the importance of handwriting and learning by hand. Forming letters helps children learn and retain information. When children are first learning to read and write, that matters.”

The second major part of Set Up for Success will be a School Start Check at ECE before children transition to primary school.

“Teachers are reporting an increasing number of new entrants are starting school lacking basic skills such as toilet training and eating and dressing independently. Children are arriving at school having never held a pencil or scissors, without the oral skills they need, and many cannot identify letters in their own name.

“To make a strong start at school, children need good foundations. The School Start Check will make those expectations clear and ECE centres will work with parents to assess how ready a child is to start school and where they may need extra support.

“This is about setting expectations, not a pass/fail test and will never stop a child starting school.

“Ensuring all young people leave school with the skills they need to secure jobs is an important part of National’s plan to fix the basics and build the future by growing the economy to create jobs, lift wages and keep taxes low.”

documents/news-260923-markmitchell.md.text:
# National’s plan to back our firefighters

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/news/260923-markmitchell> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## National’s plan to back our firefighters

23 September 2026

·

Mark Mitchell

## National’s plan to back our firefighters

Firefighters will get the equipment, training and support they deserve under National’s three-point plan to strengthen New Zealand’s fire and emergency services, National’s Emergency Management spokesperson Mark Mitchell says.

“When New Zealanders face a fire, serious crash, flood, storm or other emergency, our firefighters are there. They run towards danger to protect lives, homes and communities.

“More than 14,000 firefighters, including volunteers, paid staff, and frontline enablers, serve New Zealand around the clock. They deserve an organisation that is as reliable and prepared as they are.

“But nine years after FENZ was created, too many firefighters are still dealing with ageing trucks, breakdowns, training gaps and an organisation that is not delivering for the frontline.

“National backs our firefighters. We will reset FENZ, restore clear accountability and put frontline delivery first,” Mr Mitchell says.

National’s three-point plan will:

- Restore accountability by making FENZ a departmental agency directly accountable to the Minister for Emergency Management, removing the FENZ Board, and delivering a Turnaround Plan;

- Support volunteer firefighters by requiring FENZ to provide volunteers with additional mental and physical health support;

- Get ordered appliances into service and establish funded fleet replacement and training programmes;

- National MP Tim Costley, who initiated the select committee inquiry into FENZ fleet issues, says firefighters have too often carried the consequences of failures they did not create.

“Again and again, firefighters have found ways to keep serving their communities despite unreliable appliances, gaps in training and slow decision-making above them.

“The inquiry has shown these are not isolated problems. FENZ has spent money and purchased equipment, but it has struggled to turn those decisions into reliable capability on the frontline.

“Trucks sitting out of service do not help the crew waiting at the station, and training plans mean little if recruits are still encountering their first real fire at an emergency callout.

“This reset will put responsibility where it belongs. Fire and emergency professionals will continue making operational decisions, but there will be a clear line of accountability for whether FENZ is delivering for firefighters and communities.

“The real test is whether the appliance is ready when the alarm sounds, whether the crew has been properly trained and whether a volunteer who is injured or traumatised is properly supported.

“Our firefighters have upheld their side of the bargain. National’s plan will make sure FENZ upholds its side too,” Mr Costley says.

“Firefighters deserve reliable trucks, proper training, practical support and an organisation accountable for delivering them. A re-elected National Government will make that happen,” Mr Mitchell says.

Read more about National’s three-point plan to back firefighters and fix FENZ in the policy document HERE.

documents/news-260927-christopherluxon-1.text:
# National’s commitment to build the future for Kiwis

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/news/260927-christopherluxon-1> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## National’s commitment to build the future for Kiwis

27 September 2026

·

Christopher Luxon

## National’s commitment to build the future for Kiwis

National Leader Christopher Luxon has today given his personal commitment to New Zealanders on what National will deliver if re-elected on November 7.

“National has kept the promises we made to New Zealanders in 2023, including delivering tax relief for the first time in 14 years,” Mr Luxon says.

“After inheriting an economic recession, National’s focus on fixing the basics in the economy has helped get New Zealand growing again.

“With 2.6 per cent growth in the year to June, our economy grew faster than Australia, the United Kingdom, the United States, Canada and the European Union over the same period. That’s set to create 220,000 more jobs over the next four years.

“The previous Labour Government spent taxpayer money at one of the fastest rates in our history. Debt tripled, from $60 billion to almost $180 billion, and doubled as a share of GDP. Kiwis were left paying the price.

“Labour has shown it hasn’t learned anything and remains economically incapable of delivering the secure financial future New Zealanders have worked so hard for.

“This time, there are at least nine new taxes on the table between Labour and its prospective coalition partners. The choice for New Zealanders is between that, or no new taxes and a clear plan to fix the basics and build the future with National.

“National will continue to make the necessary choices to reprioritise wasteful spending, so we can invest in frontline services without blowing the books or needing new taxes and loading on more debt.

“In education, we’ve delivered an hour of reading, writing and maths each day, banned cell phones in class, rolled out structured literacy and maths, and will instigate a social media ban for under 16-year-olds.

“In law and order, there are 37,000 fewer victims of crime, no more gang patches, ram raids are down 85 per cent and there are more Police on the beat.

“We have brought in the biggest planning reforms in a generation, backed our farmers with commonsense changes, supported business with incentives such as Investment Boost, secured the India FTA, and increased exports by $20 billion.

“But the job is not done yet.

“This election, my commitment to New Zealanders is:

- Economic growth that delivers new jobs and higher wages

- No new taxes so you keep more of what you earn

- Compulsory KiwiSaver with higher contributions and a $1500 Baby Boost

- Paid Parental Leave extension from 26 to 30 weeks

- Better school results by replacing NCEA, regular assessment and teaching the basics brilliantly

- Tougher consequences for criminals and more Police patrols

- Faster healthcare and more medicines on top of 33 new cancer medicines already delivered

- Better infrastructure with Roads of National Significance, new classrooms and new and upgraded hospitals

- A better deal at the supermarket by driving competition

- Books in surplus so we don’t saddle our kids with new debt or more taxes.

“New Zealand can’t afford to put this all at risk with a Labour-Greens-Te Pati Māori-Opportunity Party coalition.

“If re-elected, National will continue to deliver on its plan to secure the future for all New Zealanders,” Mr Luxon says.

documents/news-260927-christopherluxon.m.title: Speech to National Party 2026 Campaign Launch
documents/news-260927-christopherluxon.m.text:
# Speech to National Party 2026 Campaign Launch

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/news/260927-christopherluxon> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## Speech to National Party 2026 Campaign Launch

27 September 2026

·

Christopher Luxon

## Speech to National Party 2026 Campaign Launch

Thank you. Thank you. Thank you.

It’s great to be with you here in Auckland today at our 2026 campaign launch.

Before I start, can I acknowledge:

Our President Sylvia Wood and Party General Manager Jo de Joux.

Thank you for your drive and dedication supporting the re-election of a National Government in this the 90 th year of our Party.

To my friend and our outstanding Deputy Leader Nicola Willis.

Our country is more prosperous, more secure, and more confident because you’ve been willing to make the tough choices – thank you.

And to all our Ministers, MPs, and candidates with us here today.

Thank you for your sacrifices – the long days and late nights, the time away from home, and for your collective determination to Fix the Basics and Build the Future.

And finally, to our members and supporters with us here today in this incredible venue!

Thank you. Thank you. Thank you.

Thank you for knocking on doors, making calls, and waving signs in the rain, because like me, you know, New Zealand needs a National Government.

While I’m here, can I also acknowledge some people who have made a massive contribution in my own life, over many years.

Mum, Dad, Amanda, William, and Olivia.

The last six years haven’t always been easy. Politics is tough and families feel all of it.

Thank you for your patience, for your support, and above all, for your unconditional love.

They say politics is a team sport. And boy, it’s a big team.

Behind the long hours, the late nights, and the time away from home, are little platoons of loved ones who make big sacrifices.

Mums and Dads. Husbands and wives. Children and grandchildren.

We couldn’t do it without them.

And I don’t just mean our team in Wellington, or our candidates around the country.

Whether you’re a Young Nat, an Indo Nat, a Pacific Blue, a Rural Nat, from our Chinese Group, or a Super Blue, our volunteers work hard.

Damn hard.

And I know how tricky it can be.

Getting to work, picking up the kids, heading to footy practice, running a business, just getting on with life, and still finding the time to don the blue jacket and knock on doors in the rain?

It’s incredible. And it’s what I love about our party.

Like me, each of you, our members and supporters, are utterly passionate about the future of our country.

Like me, you believe our best days lie ahead of us.

And like me, you believe our values are the recipe for success in a less certain and more volatile world.

Six years ago, I left a life in business and came to National because, like you, our party’s values run deep.

Strong families and caring communities.

Equal opportunity.

Competitive enterprise.

Reward for achievement.

Personal responsibility.

And from early on, those values were etched into my family life, too.

Dad worked hard. He left school and worked his way up from Sales Rep to General Manager. Dad taught me to think positively and to never let your circumstances define you or where you’re going in life.

Mum? She’s the best people person I know. She went to university the same year I did to do social work. She taught me to walk across the room and find someone different from me and to understand before I’m understood.

But together, they raised me with a determination that no matter what life throws at you, better days lie ahead.

And when I look out across the room today, I know I’m not alone.

Three years ago, we inherited a country in dire straits.

Inflation at a thirty year high.

Interest rates at their highest since the GFC.

A recession and rising unemployment.

And big deficits.

The nation’s debt had tripled, from $60 billion to $180 billion.

More than half of our young people weren’t turning up to school regularly.

Ram raids were a nightly feature on the news.

Our health system fell apart, and instead of fixing the basics for everyone, Chris Hipkins and Willie Jackson prioritised putting co-governance into the health system through a separate Māori Health Authority.

Instead of cracking down on gang offending, Jacinda Ardern and Chris Hipkins were literally handing out millions of dollars to the Mongrel Mob.

Labour lost the plot.

They spent more. They borrowed more. They taxed more.

And through it all, they lost sight of what really matters.

Your business. Your community. Your family. And your safety.

Now, they’re desperately trying to argue they’ve changed.

Do you believe them? I don’t.

The truth is that in difficult times, our country needed a National government willing to make the tough choices to get New Zealand back on track.

We needed a Minister of Finance with the guts to tackle Labour’s wasteful spending, get the books back in the black, and provide real tax relief for working Kiwis.

We needed a Minister of Justice and a Minister of Police with the guts to end Labour’s appalling track record of lawlessness and smash the gangs

We needed a Minister of Education with the guts to get our kids back to school, bring in a mobile phone ban, and get the curriculum back to the basics of reading, writing, and maths.

We needed a Minister of Trade with the guts to go out in the world and secure new trade deals to make all of us wealthier.

And we needed a Minister of Health with the guts to end Labour’s obsession with co-governance, and prioritise what really matters: more medicines, more surgeries, and more doctors.

You know, and I know, that it’s been a slog.

Our team has worked around the clock, determined to leave a legacy of success for future generations.

Replacing the RMA with a new system based on property rights.

Slashing red tape on farmers, growers, builders, plumbers, and exporters.

Ending Labour’s oil and gas ban and unleashing a tidal wave of new renewable energy.

Championing families with generational education reform, from pre-school to high school, providing every child the best possible shot at the Kiwi dream – even if the unions don’t like it.

Restoring law and order, by cracking down on gangs, putting more Police on the beat, and locking offenders up for longer to keep our community safe.

Negotiating and completing a Free Trade Agreement with India, the largest country in the world and a rapidly growing destination for Kiwi exports.

Building and delivering the infrastructure New Zealand needs to thrive, with more roads, more schools, and more hospitals.

And meanwhile, driving this country back to a financial surplus, so we can pay down Labour’s debt, and secure our future in a more volatile world.

Now after years of hard work, New Zealand is turning the corner.

Our plan, to Fix the Basics and Build the Future, is working.

Exports are booming, tourism is strong, and construction is finally turning around.

Our economy as a whole is growing, faster in the last year than the UK, the US, Australia, Canada, the EU, and Japan.

220,000 new jobs are forecast to be created in the next four years, with wages rising faster than inflation.

Crime has fallen dramatically, with 37,000 fewer victims of violent crime.

Waiting lists for surgeries and emergency care in our hospitals are falling, after they skyrocketed under Labour.

And after years of excuses, our classrooms are filling up. We now have 176,000 children back attending school regularly because we made it a priority.

And it’s extraordinary how little the Labour Party has to offer this election.

Voting opens in four weeks and on the big issues facing New Zealand, Labour has embarrassingly little to say.

On education, their only plan is a new working group.

On law and order? Nothing.

Nothing to say about the lifeblood of our economy – our farmers and growers – and no plan to lift our exports and open new markets.

Nothing to say about fast tracking new energy projects so we can keep growing our economy.

Chris Hipkins says he’s still warming up.

Well, I’ve got one simple message.

You “better start now”.

Because this country needs more than a slogan, it needs a plan.

And Labour doesn’t have one.

I could give you chapter and verse on Labour’s scandalous lack of policy, just a matter of weeks out from election day.

But I’ll cut to the chase.

You can’t afford a Labour Government.

You can’t afford nine new taxes.

You can’t afford an $18 billion hole, with no plan to pay for it.

You can’t afford a four-way coalition with 6 leaders, spearheaded by Chloe Swarbrick and Rawiri Waititi.

You can’t afford to get bribed with your own money.

You can’t afford Chris Hipkins.

Meanwhile, National is campaigning on an ambitious platform to Fix the Basics and Build the Future.

A plan that backs Kiwis at every stage of life.

From the day you’re born, to the day you get your first job, to the day you buy your first home, to the day you retire.

Let me talk you through part of our plan.

At the heart of our party is a belief that New Zealand should be a property-owning democracy.

Where every Kiwi has a real stake in the future of our economy.

And every Kiwi can look forward to a secure retirement.

That’s why we’ll supercharge KiwiSaver.

We’ll make it compulsory and we’ll lift contributions, so every Kiwi retires with a bigger nest egg.

And we’ll start from day one, ensuring every Kiwi kid starts on the road to a secure financial future, with a $1,500 Baby Boost for every child born in New Zealand.

Of course, the first months with a new baby can be challenging. Juggling time away from work and the cost of a larger family can be tough.

Well, in this party, we believe in strong families.

So National will extend paid parental leave to 30 weeks.

We’ll keep your KiwiSaver ticking over while you’re at home with your baby.

And we’ll give Mums and Dads the freedom to take their leave together.

Because how you raise your baby is a choice for your family, not for politicians and bureaucrats.

We also want our young people to build their future right here, in New Zealand.

For a young graduate, their student loan is one of the biggest bills they face.

So, we’ll reduce student loan repayments, and put more money back in the pockets of young graduates.

Every fortnight, that’s money they can use to start a small business, or put towards a deposit on a first house, instead of a ticket to Sydney or London.

And yes, we’ll come down harder on those who rort the system by leaving the country, and trying to avoid their loan altogether.

Of course, we also want those young Kiwis to own a home of their own.

Our planning reforms are already unlocking more housing with record first home buyers.

But too many young couples are still struggling to save for a deposit, even while they do everything right – working hard, paying the rent, and paying for childcare.

So National will open up 5 per cent deposit home loans to thousands more first home buyers.

Of course, to back families, we need a strong economy.

And for a small country at the bottom of the Pacific, that means selling more to the world.

New Zealand is a trading nation.

But trade isn’t just about what leaves our ports. It’s about what comes back into our communities.

More jobs, higher wages, and bigger opportunities.

We’ve already landed deals with India, the UAE, and the GCC.

Now we’re going after New Zealand’s next billion customers – in South America, in Europe, in Africa, and in Asia – so we can keep growing the economy, creating jobs, and lifting wages.

And why does that matter?

Because a strong economy means more money in your community.

A strong economy means a shot at a better life for you and your family.

A strong economy means we can afford cutting edge medicines, world-class schools and hospitals, and the infrastructure we need to keep our country moving.

A strong economy means a future for your children and grandchildren here at home.

If you want that in your heart, you need to vote with your head.

Which brings me to my personal commitment to you.

In 2023, we made promises. And we kept them.

We delivered tax relief for the first time in 14 years.

We got our kids back to the basics, with an hour of reading, writing and maths every day, and phones out of classrooms.

We brought in the biggest planning reforms in a generation, backed our farmers, signed the India FTA, and lifted exports by $20 billion.

National is the party of delivery.

But the job isn’t done yet.

So today, I’m proud to present National’s 2026 pledge card.

Ten commitments. My personal promise to every New Zealander.

Economic growth that delivers new jobs and higher wages.

No new taxes, so you keep more of what you earn.

Compulsory KiwiSaver, with higher contributions and a $1,500 Baby Boost.

Paid parental leave extended from 26 to 30 weeks.

Better school results, by replacing NCEA, regular assessment, and teaching the basics brilliantly.

Tougher consequences for criminals, and more Police patrols.

Faster healthcare and more medicines, on top of the 33 new cancer medicines we’ve already delivered.

Better infrastructure, with Roads of National Significance, new classrooms, and new and upgraded hospitals.

A better deal at the supermarket, by driving more competition.

And the books in surplus, so we don’t saddle our kids with more debt or more taxes.

Chris Hipkins has a slogan.

National has a plan.

I’m running at this election to make that a reality.

And so finally.

Look around the world today.

Wars in Europe and the Middle East. Petrol prices on fire. Rapid technological change and social upheaval.

We can’t control the world. But we can control how we respond.

At this election, New Zealanders have a choice.

A choice between no new taxes with National, and nine new taxes with Labour and their mates.

A choice between careful economic management, and a return to reckless spending.

A choice between a four-way coalition, campaigning to spend more, tax more, and borrow more, and a National-led Government, with a plan to Fix the Basics and Build the Future.

A plan to get the books back to surplus and start paying down Labour’s debt.

A plan to grow the economy and create more opportunity.

A plan for better school results.

A plan to restore law and order.

A plan to deliver faster healthcare and more medicines.

A plan for no new taxes.

If you want a National-led Government at this election, with a plan to Fix the Basics and Build the Future.

Party Vote National.

Thank you.

# National’s Economic Plan backs Kiwis to get ahead

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/news/260928-nicolawillis> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## National’s Economic Plan backs Kiwis to get ahead

28 September 2026

·

Nicola Willis

## National’s Economic Plan backs Kiwis to get ahead

National has released its Economic Plan to ensure hardworking New Zealanders can keep more of what they earn, get ahead, and build a more secure future.

The Economic Plan lays out National’s practical approach to growing the economy:

- Responsibly managing the books, including a return to surplus in 2028/29.

- Reducing red tape and supporting innovation, including the replacement of the Resource Management Act.

- Delivering world-class education, by replacing NCEA, focusing on reading, writing and maths, and delivering more trades training.

- Driving trade and investment, through securing new trade deals, boosting tourism and delivering Investment Boost.

- Building infrastructure for the future, such as new roads, hospitals, classroom and energy projects.

“Delivering on our Economic Plan means we can commit to no new taxes so people keep more of what they earn, reward hard work with more jobs and higher wages, and build New Zealanders’ financial security,” National’s Finance and Economic Growth spokesperson Nicola Willis says.

“It’s been a tough few years for everyone, with a pandemic, a recession, trade wars and global conflicts all putting pressure on Kiwi households and businesses.

“National inherited an economy in dire straits. Under Labour, inflation reached a generational high of 7.3 per cent, interest rates climbed to levels not seen since the Global Financial Crisis, and government debt tripled.

“Since coming into Government, National has been focused on reversing the downward spiral by fixing the basics in the economy. That means delivering tax relief, stopping wasteful spending to lower inflation and interest rates, and removing barriers in the way of businesses getting things done.

“Despite ongoing uncertainty overseas, New Zealand’s economy is turning around. Inflation and interest rates are down, we are growing faster than the US, UK, Canada, Australia and Japan, 220,000 new jobs are forecast over the next four years, and wages are set to grow faster than prices.

“Tomorrow’s Pre-Election Fiscal Update will provide an update on the progress we are making to reduce debt, return to surplus, grow the economy, and secure the future for New Zealanders and their families.

“National’s Economic Plan outlines the priorities and measures we will focus on to continue this progress, whether that’s supporting greater investment by growing KiwiSaver, building new Roads of National Significance and replacing NCEA, or freeing up $50 billion of government procurement to more competition and ensuring red tape isn’t holding back new fin-tech or investment.

“We need to continue with the plan that is working, especially as the world remains volatile. Now is not the time to dramatically change course by loading on more spending, more taxes and more borrowing as Labour is proposing.

“The only way to keep the momentum going is with a National-led Government and a clear plan to strengthen the economy so Kiwis can get ahead.

“We will continue to get the books in order, reduce red tape and support innovation, improve education, drive trade and investment, and build the infrastructure New Zealand needs. It’s all part of our wider plan to fix the basics and build the future.

“The choice is clear this election. It’s either National which is fixing the basics and building the future by growing the economy to create more jobs and higher wages with no new taxes, or a chaotic Labour coalition that spends more, increases debt and imposes at least nine new taxes that will make every Kiwi worse off.”

# National to trial seamless trans-Tasman travel

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/news/261001-national-to-trial-seamless-trans-tasman> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## National to trial seamless trans-Tasman travel

01 October 2026

·

Louise Upston

A re-elected National Government will work with Australia to trial seamless travel for Australian and New Zealand citizens travelling between the two countries.

National Party Tourism spokesperson, Louise Upston says it is the next logical step between countries that share two of the most closely integrated economies in the world.

“Making it easier for Australians to visit New Zealand means more visitors exploring our cities and regions which results in more incomes for local businesses, more jobs opportunities for New Zealanders, and a stronger economy,” Ms Upston says.

National has already put the foundations in place. In 2009, the National-led Government officially launched SmartGate for trans-Tasman passengers. This was the first step in streamlining travel between the two countries.

In 2024, Prime Ministers Luxon and Albanese endorsed the work of the Trans-Tasman Seamless Travel Group and committed to exploring ways to move closer to seamless travel between the two countries.

“We will deliver on that commitment. The 2028 ICC Men’s T20 World Cup will be jointly hosted by Australia and New Zealand from 21 October to 19 November that year. National will work to introduce a trial prior to the T20.

“This would look like a fully digital trans-Tasman travel experience, where eligible travellers can rely on a smartphone, digital credentials and biometric technology through more of the airport journey.

“This would mean no paper passport required at the gate and faster movement through airports, while maintaining the security and integrity of New Zealand’s border and preserving the ability of border agencies to intervene where risk is identified,” Ms Upston says.

“Growing New Zealand’s tourism industry is a critical part of National’s plan to fix the basics and build the future. Tourism is our second-largest export earner and supports around one in nine jobs.

“Today’s announcement is in the spirit of the long-standing and close relationship between our two countries and will make passage between them as seamless as possible, whilst still maintaining the security and integrity of New Zealand’s border.”

# Affordable power Kiwis can rely on

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/news/261002-simeonbrown> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## Affordable power Kiwis can rely on

02 October 2026

·

Simeon Brown

## Affordable power Kiwis can rely on

National's nine-point energy plan will tackle the costs pushing up power bills and build a more secure energy future for New Zealand, National's Energy spokesperson Simeon Brown says.

"Secure, affordable power is key to keeping homes warm, keeping businesses competitive, and supporting the growth that creates jobs and lifts wages," Mr Brown says.

"A re-elected National Government will build on our success this term with Electrify NZ 2.0, a nine-point plan delivering more supply, more competition, and more choice for households and businesses, to help make power more affordable."

Under Electrify NZ 2.0, a re-elected National Government will:

- Unlock new energy development zones by letting developers, major users, and investors build transmission and recover costs from those who use them.

- Make connections faster and cheaper by allowing Kiwis to choose an accredited contractor, not just the one their network hands them.

- Let Kiwis sell power to the best buyer, so households and businesses with solar or a battery can sell to any power company, not just the one they buy from.

- Address the dry year problem by levelling the playing field for backup power by opening the backup market.

- Tackle lines charges by reviewing the rules that set them to make necessary changes, and require residential and small business solar connections to be approved within two working days.

- Make affordability a core objective for the Electricity Authority by writing it into law.

- Cut more red tape holding back renewables so wind, solar, and hydro can be built faster.

- Launch the Home Energy Fund, giving Kiwis low-interest, long-term loans to invest in their own power and cut their own bills, and enable plug-in solar.

- Require AI data centres to bring their own new, firmed power, so new digital investment adds to the grid and creates jobs instead of pushing up prices.

"New Zealand is experiencing its biggest renewables boom in a generation under National, with more new renewable generation built in the past three years than in the previous eight," Mr Brown says. "That's helped lower the price power companies pay for electricity, with significant reductions in wholesale prices in the past year. That supports businesses, and puts households on a path to more affordable power.

"But the price of electricity itself is only one part of a power bill. Lines charges, red tape, weak competition, and the cost of keeping the lights on in a dry year all add to what Kiwis pay. Our nine-point plan takes on each of them.

"Lines charges accounted for around two-thirds of the rise in the average power bill over the past year. They're set under an outdated law, so we'll review it and make necessary changes ahead of the next price reset. We’ll also let Kiwis choose who does the connection work they're paying for.

"Red tape is holding back new power at every scale, even on people's own land. Environment Canterbury has required a consent for ground-mounted solar panels in case rain washes bird droppings off them. That's the kind of red tape we'll scrap.

"Reliability matters too. We need backup for when the lakes are low, but a few big power companies hold most of it, largely for their own use, and smaller power companies have no easy way to buy the backup they need to get through a dry year.

"We've already moved to give independent retailers fairer access to the contracts they need to compete with the big players. Opening up backup supply is the next step to levelling the playing field.

"New demand needs new supply too, so AI data centres will need to bring their own power rather than push up bills for everyone else.

"This term we've reversed Labour's oil and gas ban, scrapped Lake Onslow and the 100 per cent renewables target that put investors off, and sped up approvals for new power projects. We've also built up strategic fuel reserves at Huntly and started the process to deliver an LNG import facility, so a dry year is managed rather than a crisis. Electrify NZ 2.0 will build on that progress.

"Labour would put all of that progress at risk. Chris Hipkins has promised to bring back the oil and gas exploration ban, which would drive investment and jobs offshore and send power prices soaring.

"Higher power bills would come on top of the $2,263 a year in extra tax that Labour's spending promises would cost the average household. "This election is going to be incredibly close. The choice is clear, between National with a nine-point energy plan to support more affordable power, with no new taxes. Or a Labour coalition that would push power prices up and leave Kiwis worse off with nine new taxes."

documents/news-261004-chrisbishop.md.text:
# Mill Road Stage One given the green light

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/news/261004-chrisbishop> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## Mill Road Stage One given the green light

04 October 2026

·

Chris Bishop

## Mill Road Stage One given the green light

The next National-led government will start construction on Stage One of Mill Road and progress route protection on Stages Two and Three, National’s Transport Spokesperson Chris Bishop says.

“Mill Road is an important Road of National Significance that is part of the Government’s Major Transport Projects Pipeline, included in the Auckland City Deal as well as NZTA’s Auckland Strategic Motorway Plan,” Mr Bishop says.

“South Auckland is one of the fastest-growing parts of the country and Drury is at the centre of that growth, but the roading network hasn’t kept up.

“People travelling between Drury, Papakura and Manukau are funnelled onto an already congested Southern Motorway, while roads like Redoubt Road and the existing Mill Road were built for a semi-rural community, not tens of thousands of new households.

“Mill Road will change that. Once complete, it will be a new four-lane, 21.5-kilometre corridor running alongside State Highway 1 from Manukau to Drury, crushing congestion, improving safety, and unlocking land for the homes and jobs the region needs.

“Mill Road Stage One, between Manukau and Alfriston, is one of the highest-ranked projects on the Government’s Major Transport Projects Pipeline. It has a Benefit-Cost Ratio of 3.1 if not tolled, or 2.2 if tolled.

“NZTA estimates Stage One will reduce congestion by 30 per cent on the corridor, cut journey times by 25 per cent, and result in a more than 60 per cent reduction in deaths and serious injuries.

“National will allocate $1.75 billion in Budget 2028 so construction can begin in the late-2028 construction season.

"We've made strong progress on Mill Road Stage One over the last three years. The NZTA Board has endorsed the investment case, and NZTA is completing the design work and taking the project through the fast-track process to secure the consents it needs.

“After years of debate and discussion about Mill Road, National in government is getting on with it.

“In addition to starting construction on Stage One, National will allocate $100 million to progress route protection on Stages Two and Three.

“Landowners, Auckland Council, businesses and communities need certainty about where the future corridor will go, so they can plan and make investment decisions with confidence. Route protection will provide that certainty and ensure the corridor can ultimately be completed from Manukau through to Drury.”

“The commitment to Mill Road builds on the strong progress National has made on transport across Auckland over the last three years, including opening the City Rail Link, progressing the Eastern Busway and Northwest Rapid Transit, investing in the Third Main and rail electrification, delivering new rail stations and level crossing removals, and reforming Auckland’s transport governance so there is clearer accountability for how the city’s transport network is planned and delivered.

“We’re building the transport infrastructure Auckland needs for the future.

“National has a plan to grow the economy, spend sensibly and get debt down, with no new taxes. A Labour coalition would squander surpluses, hike debt and hit Kiwis with nine new taxes to pay for its spending plans – and that would mean every household paying $2263 in extra tax every year,” Mr Bishop says.

National’s Mill Road Policy here

documents/news-261005-chrisbishop.md.text:
# Belfast to Pegasus & Woodend Bypass given green light

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/news/261005-chrisbishop> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## Belfast to Pegasus & Woodend Bypass given green light

05 October 2026

·

Chris Bishop

## Belfast to Pegasus & Woodend Bypass given green light

A re-elected National government will fully fund the Belfast to Pegasus Motorway and Woodend Bypass, with $800 million committed in our first Budget so construction can begin next year, National’s Transport Spokesperson Chris Bishop says.

“This is the next major transport project Canterbury needs, and National will fund it so NZTA can get on and build it,” Mr Bishop says.

“The Belfast to Pegasus Motorway and Woodend Bypass will extend the Christchurch Northern Motorway around 11 kilometres north, from just south of the Waimakariri River to beyond Pegasus and Ravenswood.

“Canterbury is the engine room of the South Island. It is home to around 695,000 people, roughly one in eight New Zealanders, and is our second-largest regional economy, generating $55.5 billion of GDP in the year to March 2025.

“North Canterbury is one of the places where that growth is being felt most strongly. The Waimakariri District has more than doubled in size since the early 1990s to around 70,000 people, while Woodend, Pegasus and Ravenswood continue to grow rapidly.

“SH1 approaching Woodend already carries around 21,500 vehicles a day, around nine per cent of them freight, and that is expected to increase to around 28,000 vehicles a day by 2048.

“That pressure is being felt in Woodend itself. At peak times it can take up to 20 minutes to travel through the town, while heavy through-traffic makes it harder for locals to access shops, schools and other parts of the community.

“There is also a significant safety problem. Between 2014 and 2023 there were 280 crashes on SH1 through Woodend, including three fatalities and 25 serious injuries.

“The new motorway and bypass will fundamentally change how this corridor works. The project includes widening the southern section of SH1 from two to four lanes, a new four-lane motorway bypass to the north, major intersection upgrades and new bridges.

“NZTA estimates the project will save motorists up to 10 minutes at peak times, reduce traffic through Woodend from around 21,500 vehicles a day to 8,000, and reduce deaths and serious injuries by 78 per cent.

“For locals, the bypass means getting their town centre back. Moving through-traffic and heavy trucks onto the new motorway will make Woodend safer, easier to get around and a better place for local businesses and the community.

“It will also make the corridor more reliable for people and freight travelling to and from Christchurch, Christchurch Airport and Lyttelton Port.

“This is not a project starting from scratch. Because of National’s work in government, the project is ready to go and is the next investment-ready project on the Major Transport Projects Pipeline.

“National will commit $800 million in our first Budget to fully fund the Belfast to Pegasus Motorway and Woodend Bypass, allowing construction to commence in 2027.

“National has already increased transport investment in Canterbury to $1.8 billion, around 50 per cent more than under Labour.

“We will continue making the choices needed to invest in the infrastructure New Zealand needs to grow.

“National has a plan to grow the economy, spend sensibly and get debt down, with no new taxes. A Labour coalition would squander surpluses, hike debt and hit Kiwis with nine new taxes to pay for its spending plans – and that would mean every household paying $2263 in extra tax every year,” Mr Bishop says.

documents/news-261006-simeonbrown.md.text:
# More medicines for Kiwis at home

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/news/261006-simeonbrown> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## More medicines for Kiwis at home

06 October 2026

·

Simeon Brown

## More medicines for Kiwis at home

A re-elected National Government will put New Zealand patients first, bringing money back from overseas to fund more medicines and expand cancer screening, National's Health spokesperson Simeon Brown says.

"National has put patients back at the heart of the health system, delivering the largest ever boost for new medicines and expanding free screening nationwide. Now we want to go further, getting more medicines to Kiwis and catching cancer early, when it is most treatable," Mr Brown says.

A re-elected National Government will:

- Deliver a further $604 million uplift in Pharmac's medicines budget

- Turn responsible fiscal management into more medicines by reducing foreign aid outside the Pacific and making MFAT more efficient

- Set a national target for clinical trials in New Zealand

- Unlock CAR-T cell therapy

"When National came into Government, Labour had left behind a funding cliff in Pharmac's budget. We filled that gap, then went further with a record $604 million investment, delivering 66 new medicines benefiting hundreds of thousands of Kiwis, including 33 new cancer treatments.

"But new treatments become available overseas every year, so National will invest a further $604 million to help Pharmac fund more new medicines and widen access to those already funded.

"We will largely pay for it by reducing foreign aid and associated administration costs by 10 per cent, while fully protecting aid to the Pacific.

"New Zealanders are generous people, and we'll continue to play our part in the world. But National believes more of New Zealanders' hard-earned money should be spent here at home, caring for Kiwis fighting cancer and other serious illnesses, rather than being sent offshore.

"Clinical trials and CAR-T also give New Zealanders access to cutting-edge treatments, often years before they would otherwise be available. For someone facing cancer or a rare disorder, that can mean real hope when other options have run out.”

A re-elected National Government will also:

- Lower the free bowel screening age to 50 by 2029

- Complete the free breast screening extension to age 74 by 2029

- Launch new screening pilots for prostate and lung cancer

- Deliver free cervical screening for all women aged 25 to 69 from March 2027

- Establish the Healthy Kiwis Programme, offering active prescriptions

"Early detection and prevention are just as important, catching cancer when it is most treatable and keeping more Kiwis well and out of hospital.

"National has already lowered the bowel screening age twice in just a year, from 60 to 58 and now to 56, moving as fast as we safely can. We will keep going until we reach 50 by 2029, with more colonoscopy capacity to match.

"For women, we are making cervical screening free for those aged 25 to 69 and finishing the job of extending free breast screening to 74.

"But there is still no organised screening programme for prostate cancer, the most common cancer in New Zealand men, or for lung cancer, our biggest cancer killer. The pilots will test the best way to screen for both, building the evidence for potential nationwide programmes.

"Beyond cancer, the Healthy Kiwis Programme will help stop chronic diseases like type 2 diabetes before they start, with a target to double the number of people receiving active prescriptions by 2030.

"Supporting families through some of the hardest moments of their lives is why National has been so focused on responsible financial management, so we can keep investing in the health services that matter most.

"This election is going to be very tight, and the choice could not be clearer. It's either a Labour coalition that would hit Kiwis with nine new taxes. Or National, who will put the health of Kiwis at home ahead of money sent overseas, delivering more medicines and earlier screening with no new taxes," Mr Brown says.

# Small business backed with 47-point Plan

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/news/261007-cameronbrewer> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## Small business backed with 47-point Plan

07 October 2026

·

Cameron Brewer

## Small business backed with 47-point Plan

National is supporting small businesses with a 47-point Small Business Plan to reduce compliance costs and make it easier to invest, grow and employ staff, National’s Small Business spokesperson Cameron Brewer says.

“Small businesses make up around 97 per cent of all New Zealand enterprises. Around 600,000 businesses employ approximately 680,000 people.

“Behind those numbers are owners, workers and families whose ambition and effort help drive our economy. “National will back those businesses to succeed. We want the sole trader to feel confident taking on an apprentice, the café owner to open a second premises, and the local manufacturer to win their first overseas order. “When small businesses can invest, employ and grow, the benefits flow to their communities, with more jobs and more opportunities to get ahead. “National’s 47-point Small Business Plan will make doing business easier by:

- Delivering a Tell Government Once service built around the New Zealand Business Number and existing government systems including Inland Revenue, ACC, the Companies Office and relevant licensing bodies.

- A fast track for straightforward disputes within the Employment Relations Authority, for suitable minor employment disputes.

- Reviewing the compulsory GST registration threshold, which has remained at $60,000 since 2009.

- Rewriting priority health and safety codes and guidance in plain English, with practical examples for small businesses.

- Helping more small and medium Kiwi businesses succeed overseas by backing the next 200 high-potential exporters with intensive support.

- Making repeat seasonal hiring easier with a standard recurring seasonal agreement and shorter renewal process.

- Keeping Investment Boost, protecting the immediate 20 per cent deduction that backs businesses to invest, grow and hire.

“A big part of our Small Business Plan is simplifying employment rules so it is easier to take on new staff and create more opportunities in small businesses’ communities,” Mr Brewer says. “The First Employee Support Package will deliver practical, dedicated advice for new employers through first year of their first hire - employment agreement tools, payroll guidance, and tax and ACC reminders. “Small businesses don’t have teams of people to deal with government paperwork. Often it is the owner doing everything themselves late at night after the kids are in bed. “That is why this plan is focused on practical changes that give them time back, whether that is helping them through their first hire, resolving employment disputes faster, or letting them update core business information once instead of repeating it across government.” “National backs the Kiwis who put their savings, livelihoods and ambition into building a business. Investment Boost supports businesses to invest in better equipment, expand their premises or take on more work. That creates opportunities for their staff and their communities. Labour wants to take it away. “National knows the only way to create jobs and help Kiwis get ahead is to grow the economy, spend sensibly and get debt down, with no new taxes. Backing small businesses to succeed is a key part of how we make that happen.”

# Firm, fair, affordable welfare

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/news/261008-louiseupston> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## Firm, fair, affordable welfare

08 October 2026

·

Louise Upston

## Firm, fair, affordable welfare

A re-elected National Government will ensure the welfare system remains focused on employment and is fair and affordable for taxpayers, National’s Social Development and Employment spokesperson Louise Upston says.

“National believes those who can work should work. Employment is the best way out of hardship, giving people more independence, choices and opportunities. Our welfare system provides a safety net when people need it, but it must be fair and affordable for hardworking taxpayers who fund it.

“In government, National has focused on getting more people off welfare and into work, after Labour let long-term dependency grow. We’ve provided support and training for Jobseekers, while also driving expectations and consequences.

“If re-elected, National will build on this with a new five-point plan that includes the introduction of random drug testing from next year, as part of MSD’s work-readiness. It will start with 10,000 tests in the first year and expand over time.

“Our economy is growing and there are 220,000 more jobs expected over the next four years. We want every Kiwi on Jobseeker to be ready to take up available jobs, including in industries where passing a drug test is a condition of employment.

“We know there’s more to do, so along with random drug testing we’re highlighting four other new initiatives today.”

- Investing earlier to help long-term Jobseekers into work. National will provide more intensive, work-focused support for 30,000 work-ready jobseekers who have been on Jobseeker for more than a year, before long-term dependency becomes entrenched, with greater funding for employment programmes that support young people into work.

- Stronger expectations after two years. From 1 April 2028, those who have received Jobseeker for two of the previous three years will move to a lower rate of payment, with a smaller reduction for households with dependent children.

- Double the stand-down for repeated voluntary unemployment. People who repeatedly leave employment without good and sufficient reason will face a 26-week non-entitlement period, up from 13 weeks.

- Extending the benefit residency requirement to five years. From 1 April 2028, the minimum residence period to qualify for main benefits will increase from two years to five years.

“For many New Zealanders drug testing is already a normal part of their employment so it’s entirely reasonable for work-ready Jobseekers to meet the same basic expectations.

“Under our policy, a first failed test will be recorded and a second failed test will trigger a clinical alcohol and drug assessment. Where someone then fails to meet their obligations, the normal sanctions regime will apply, which could include reductions to their benefit.

“This isn’t about punishing someone because they haven't found a job. It’s about making sure people receiving Jobseeker Support meet reasonable expectations to be ready for work, which also helps ensure it is fair to hardworking taxpayers who fund the system.

“Our five-point plan will provide more help to get into work, and stronger expectations and consequences the longer someone remains on welfare or repeatedly makes choices that keep them out of work.

“It’s part of National’s wider economic plan, which sees us continue to spend sensibly and get debt down, with no new taxes. A Labour coalition would squander surpluses, hike debt and hit Kiwis with nine new taxes to pay for its spending plans – and that would mean every household paying $2263 in extra tax every year.”

documents/news-261009-toddmcclay-1.md.title: Securing water and fertiliser to back NZ farmers
documents/news-261009-toddmcclay-1.md.text:
# Securing water and fertiliser to back NZ farmers

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/news/261009-toddmcclay-1> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## Securing water and fertiliser to back NZ farmers

09 October 2026

·

Todd McClay

·

Mike Butterick

## Securing water and fertiliser to back NZ farmers

A re-elected National Government will make security of New Zealand’s water and fertiliser a priority for New Zealand farmers, National’s Agriculture spokesperson Todd McClay and Associate Agriculture spokesperson Mike Butterick say.

Security of supply is critical to enable our farmers to produce food and generate the exports that are currently worth $65.2 billion to New Zealand’s economy.

“Water is one of New Zealand’s greatest strategic and natural advantages. It supports regional jobs and earns the export earnings that pay for our hospitals, our schools and our roads,” Mr McClay says.

“New Zealand receives more rainfall per person than almost any developed nation on earth, yet too many of our regions still face real water insecurity, because it often arrives in the wrong places and in the wrong seasons.

“When farmers and growers have reliable water, they produce more, take on more staff and more money flows into the local town, which means more jobs and stronger exports.

“At present, New Zealand only captures and uses about two per cent of our total annual rainfall. There is an additional 400,000 hectares ready for irrigation right now, waiting on water storage projects to be built and resource consents to be granted,” Mr McClay says.

If re-elected, National will secure New Zealand’s greatest natural asset for the next generation by:

- Committing $300 million in concessional loans to get water storage built, starting with five prioritised projects.

- Delivering New Zealand’s first long-term water infrastructure pipeline, in partnership with growers, farmers, councils and iwi.

- Publishing the first National Rural and Provincial Water Use Strategy in 2027, backed by a national storage register.

- Introducing a National Standard for on-farm and other lower-risk off-stream water storage

- Introducing a National Standard for irrigation, to make consenting easier for farmers and growers.

Mike Butterick says fertiliser is equally important to agriculture.

“Without reliable access, our farming sector could not sustain anything close to its current production base.

“New Zealand plans for fuel security and energy security. National believes we should also plan for fertiliser security to protect New Zealand’s productive economy.

“National will prioritise reducing reliance on imports and improve certainty of availability for our farmers, Mr Butterick says.

National will:

- Negotiate fertiliser security agreements, using the AOTES blueprint, with key supplier countries to protect New Zealand-bound product from export restrictions, provide early warning of supply disruptions and greater supply-chain, and keep essential nutrients flowing to our farmers.

- Introduce a $10 million Critical Inputs Fund to partner with domestic fertiliser manufacturers to support pathways for long-term domestic nitrogen production and the transition from natural gas to electrification.

“National backs farmers as part of our plan to grow the economy, spend sensibly and get debt down, with no new taxes. A Labour coalition would squander surpluses, hike debt and hit Kiwis with nine new taxes to pay for its spending plans – and that would mean households paying $2263 in extra tax every year,” Mr McClay says.

documents/news-261010-toddmcclay.md.text:
# National’s plan for healthy fisheries

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/news/261010-toddmcclay> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## National’s plan for healthy fisheries

10 October 2026

·

Todd McClay

·

Tama Potaka

## National’s plan for healthy fisheries

National’s fisheries plan backs the health of the Hauraki Gulf, the right of recreational fishers to continue the Kiwi tradition of catching a feed, and provides for sustainable seafood to be caught for our fish and chip shops and exports, National’s Oceans and Fisheries spokesperson Todd McClay and Conservation spokesperson Tama Potaka, say.

The policy creates a new marine reserve in the Hauraki Gulf and further expands the size of the Goat Island Marine Reserve.

“The New Zealand seafood industry’s economic output is around $6.4 billion, our recreational fishers generate around $1.7 billion of economic activity each year, and the annual worth of the boating and marine industry is around $3 billion.

“All fishers, commercial and recreational, depend on the health of our waters, so that is an important part of our plan,” Mr McClay says.

If re-elected, National will:

- Establish a new marine reserve off Waiheke Island and further expand the size of Goat Island /Te Hāwere-a-Maki Marine Reserve.

- Support recreational fishers – ensuring fishers have a seat at the table in fishing reforms, ruling out a recreational fishing licence and preventing the commercial sale of marlin.

- Ban commercial fishing in Hauraki Gulf’s High Protection Areas and review designated trawl corridors.

- Invest in innovation – with a $20 million Fish Tech Innovation Fund

- Increase protection of the EEZ and preserve our seamounts with an aim to increase protected areas from 32% to 50% by 2040.

- Keep the ban on shellfish and marine species from rockpools to support the recovery and impose higher penalties and strict enforcement.

- Increase the number of Honorary Fisheries Officers to 200.

- Increase penalties and infringements for exceeding catch limits

Tama Potaka says National's approach is custodianship.

“It’s about understanding the asset, managing it well, and handing it on in better condition than we found it.

“We know the health of our ocean matters to every New Zealander. It is part of who we are, provides us food, recreation, well-being, and a place for families and communities to connect,” Tama Potaka says.

Todd McClay says commercial fishing is an important part of New Zealand’s economy.

“It supports thousands of jobs in coastal communities and provides high-quality, locally caught seafood for New Zealanders and export markets alike, with close to $2 billion in annual export earnings. While some people catch their own fish, most New Zealanders enjoy seafood from their local supermarket or fish and chip shop. Ensuring the longterm sustainability of our fisheries is critical for both coastal communities and consumers.

“In National’s first term of government, we passed the Hauraki Gulf / Tīkapa Moana Marine Protection Act 2025, the most significant expansion of marine protection in more than a decade.

“We also delivered five new marine reserves as part of the South-East Marine Protection Network, Te Au Roao Te Rakihouia protecting 308 square kilometres of unique marine habitat and sea life.

“This election will be tight and the choice is clear. A Labour coalition wants to tax everything from the family bach to the land it sits on. They will squander surpluses, hike debt and hit Kiwis with nine new taxes that will impact everyone.

“National will protect the things Kiwis care about and continue our plan to grow the economy, spend sensibly and get debt down, with no new taxes.”

# National will lift school leaving requirements

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/news/261011-ericastanford> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## National will lift school leaving requirements

11 October 2026

·

Erica Stanford

## National will lift school leaving requirements

A re-elected National Government will require students to stay at school until they complete Year 11 giving more young people time to build the knowledge and skills they need for a successful future, National’s Education spokesperson Erica Stanford says.

“Currently, students can leave school when they turn 16. Many reach that birthday during Year 11, allowing them to leave before completing the year.

“National is scrapping NCEA and from 2028 will begin replacing it with new national qualifications that are clearer and more credible and will give students, parents and employers confidence in what young people know and can do.

“With these new qualifications, our expectation is clear. Students should complete at least a full Year 11 of compulsory science, English and maths, and have the opportunity to gain the new Foundational Award in literacy and numeracy.

“Strong literacy and numeracy skills give young people a better chance of gaining employment or continuing on into Trades’ training or other learning. This change will mean more students stay at school longer and complete that important year of study.”

Ms Stanford says students will still be able to apply for a leaving exemption if they have found a job or are moving into further training.

“What we don’t want is 16-year-olds dropping out of school with nothing to do but sit on the couch. These new requirements will help young people get the skills they need to get a job or into further learning.”

National will also set nationally consistent start and finish dates for schools.

“Parents have told us how frustrating it is when their children attend different schools with different start and finish dates, leaving them juggling childcare and taking extra leave from work. So, we will work with schools on a more consistent calendar.”

Ms Stanford says National’s focus on teaching the basics brilliantly is beginning to deliver results.

“We have introduced an hour a day each of reading, writing and maths, mandated structured literacy, backed teachers with training and resources, and made the largest investment in learning support in a generation.

“We are seeing encouraging improvements in phonics, Year 6 maths and writing. Now we are getting on with replacing NCEA and making sure young people have the time to gain the skills and qualifications they need.

“National will keep the focus on raising achievement and closing the equity gap, so every young person has the opportunity to succeed at school and go on to live the life they want.”

### Notes to editors:

- Students will need to remain at school until they complete Year 11 or turn 16, whichever is later, unless an exemption applies.

- In 2025, 1,106 early leaving exemptions were approved: 90.1 per cent for further education or training and 9.9 per cent for employment.

- The Foundational Award will be introduced in 2028, followed by the New Zealand Certificate of Education at Year 12 in 2029 and the New Zealand Advanced Certificate of Education at Year 13 in 2030.

# National’s plan to secure New Zealand’s future

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/news/261012-nicolawillis> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## National’s plan to secure New Zealand’s future

12 October 2026

·

Nicola Willis

## National’s plan to secure New Zealand’s future

National’s fiscal plan prioritises bringing down debt and delivers surplus in 2028/29, with no new taxes, Finance and Economic Growth spokesperson Nicola Willis says.

“New Zealanders have worked hard through a tough few years. National’s plan is about rewarding that hard work, letting more of what people earn stay in their pockets, and building a more secure future for families and businesses.

“Our plan will set New Zealand up for the future and put us in a stronger position to withstand the next severe weather event, natural disaster or global shock.

“Getting debt down is essential to delivering lasting prosperity for New Zealand.

“Less debt helps keep inflation and interest rates down, which means lower mortgage and business borrowing costs. That gives households more breathing room in their budget, and businesses the confidence to invest, build and hire.

“It also gives the government more space to keep investing in frontline services that New Zealanders rely on, without new taxes.

“While our fiscal plan shows a pathway to potential tax relief for working New Zealanders, now is not the time to cut taxes. National’s priority is to get on top of the debt first so that our kids and grandkids aren’t left with a bigger bill and to ensure we have a bigger buffer to withstand future global shocks.

“National’s fiscal plan includes costings for every election commitment, setting aside funding to deliver priorities such as extending paid parental leave to 30 weeks, the $1500 KiwiSaver Baby Boost and lower student loan repayments.

“It also reflects expected savings from reductions in foreign aid and welfare expenditure. The net fiscal impact of National’s election commitments, outside of health cost pressure funding, is $470 million on average per annum.

“Our fiscal plan also ensures that we invest in the frontline public services that Kiwis rely on. “We have set aside a total of $15.4 billion for additional health investment over the next four years, which includes National’s medicines and bowel screening election commitments. That still leaves $7.5 billion for other cost pressures and new initiatives, including the usual yearly uplifts for areas like education and policing.

“National’s track record is strong. In each of our first three Budgets, National kept spending within the operating allowances we committed to in our 2023 fiscal plan.

“This plan is a continuation of the work we’ve done in government. After inheriting a very difficult set of books from Labour, where debt had tripled and government spending increased 70 per cent, National has been rebuilding the economy.

“We have fixed the basics by delivering income tax relief and controlling spending to ease pressure on inflation and interest rates. At the same time, we’ve been building a more secure future for New Zealand by creating opportunities for more growth through things like trade deals, Investment Boost, and planning reforms.

“Despite ongoing turmoil overseas, our plan is working. New Zealand’s economy is turning the corner and the hard work of households and businesses over the last three years is paying off.”

The latest forecasts show an operating surplus of $4.0 billion in 2028/29, growing to $11.7 billion in 2030/31. Net core Crown debt peaks at 43.9 per cent of GDP in 2027/28, then falls to 39.5 per cent by 2030/31. Wages are set to grow faster than prices and 220,000 new jobs are expected over the next four years.

“National is the party of low tax. We delivered income tax relief for working New Zealanders for the first time in 14 years and we are committing to no new taxes if re-elected. On the other hand, Labour and its coalition partners have proposed at least nine new taxes which will cost the average household $2263 a year.

“National’s approach has got us this far, but our plan needs three more years to bed in. That is how we help Kiwis secure their future.”

# National’s plan to welcome more Kiwis home

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/news/261013-nicolawillis> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## National’s plan to welcome more Kiwis home

13 October 2026

·

Nicola Willis

## National’s plan to welcome more Kiwis home

A re-elected National Government will legislate and direct five key commitments in its first 100 days aimed at encouraging young New Zealanders to stay or return home to build their future, Finance and Economic Growth spokesperson Nicola Willis says.

“National wants to make New Zealand the most attractive place for our young people to raise a family, build a career, start a business, and make a contribution to our country.

“If re-elected, National will legislate and direct five key commitments in our first 100 days to make New Zealand more attractive and affordable for young people to live and work.”

These five commitments are:

- Lowering student loan repayment rates for Kiwis living in New Zealand so they have more take-home pay when they need it most

- Widening access to 5 per cent deposits for first home buyers so more people can overcome the barrier of the standard 20 per cent deposit

- Extending paid parental leave from 26 weeks to 30 weeks within three years so that parents have more financial security while caring for their baby

- Strengthening KiwiSaver, including a $1500 Baby Boost payment and changes to contributions for parents on paid parental leave, so people can build bigger savings nest eggs to ensure greater financial security

- Prioritising and expediting work and visitor visas for partners of New Zealand citizens, so Kiwis who meet their partners overseas can bring them home when they return.

Each commitment has been fully funded to commence by 1 July 2027 in National’s fiscal plan (some may be earlier). Where a legislative change is needed to implement a commitment, National will pass the legislation in its first 100 days.

“National has also committed to no new taxes, because helping hardworking Kiwis keep more of what they earn is a key part of our proposition for young people,” Nicola Willis says.

“That is also why in 2024 we delivered income tax relief, giving average households with children an extra $78 a fortnight, and why we have been focused on keeping costs down by controlling spending to reduce debt and ease pressure on inflation and interest rates.

“New Zealand’s lack of a capital gains tax is a real competitive advantage over Australia, and we should embrace that by not introducing one.

“We want Kiwis living overseas to be excited about the opportunities New Zealand presents for them to get ahead and build a more secure future. Delivering those opportunities means growing the economy with things like new trade deals, a world-class education system and modern, reliable infrastructure.

“We have made a lot of progress. We are growing faster than the US, the UK, Canada, and Australia. Exports are up $20 billion, inflation is down from a 32-year high, and 220,000 new jobs are expected with wages growing faster than prices.

“It is encouraging to see more Kiwis returning home, with a 14 per cent increase in Kiwis moving back to New Zealand from Australia last year. But there is more to do and that means sticking with National’s plan which is working.

“The alternative is a Labour Government propped up by the Greens, Te Pati Māori and Opportunity, planning nine new taxes and more of the same mistakes Labour made last time that forced Kiwis to leave in the first place.

“If young New Zealanders want a more secure future, they should stick with the plan and party vote National.”
