# Plan for Hunting and Fishing

Published by the New Zealand National Party as a PDF policy document. Source: <https://assets.national.org.nz/web/prod/Plan%20for%20Hunting%20and%20Fishing.pdf?v=1785037436>.
The text below is the verbatim text layer of the PDF extracted with `pdftotext` (reading order). Line breaks follow the
PDF; tables and multi-column layouts may read out of order in this section, so a second rendering that preserves the
page layout (`pdftotext -layout`) follows it. Nothing has been added, removed or paraphrased.

## Full text (reading order)

Building the Future: Our Plan for Hunting
and Fishing
Hunting and fishing are part of the Kiwi way of life. They put food on the table,
bring families and communities together, support regional jobs and tourism,
and connect New Zealanders with the outdoors.
Over this term, National has given hunters and fishers
a stronger voice in government and delivered practical
progress to improve access and game management.
A re-elected National Government will build on this by:
•

recognising valued introduced species in law;

•

  stablishing a clearer framework for wild animal
e
management;

•

s  trengthening the Game Animal Council and
modernise Fish & Game;

•

  xpanding hunter-led conservation and protect
e
recreational access; and

•

 growing hunting-related jobs and exports.

Recognising valued introduced species
New Zealand’s wild animals are managed through
a fragmented collection of laws, agencies and plans.
Responsibilities are often unclear, while species valued
by hunters, anglers and local communities can be
treated simply as pests.
A re-elected National Government will establish a
coordinated wild animal management framework and
formally recognise valued introduced species in law.
This will include introduced species that provide
recreational, economic, environmental or cultural value
to New Zealanders. They will not be treated as pests
by default simply because they were introduced.
Management will remain practical and evidence
based. Action will still be taken where populations
cause unacceptable environmental damage,
but species will be managed according to
local conditions.

Strengthen the Game Animal Council and Fish
& Game
National will strengthen the Game Animal Council
as the statutory manager of valued game animals.
The Council will have a clearer role in managing
herds of special interest, developing national and
regional game animal management plans, and
supporting practical hunter-led conservation. It
will also help coordinate recreational, guided and
commercial hunting on public conservation land,
improving monitoring and reducing conflict between
different users.
National will also pass legislation to modernise Fish
& Game New Zealand. The reforms will simplify
administration, strengthen accountability to licence
holders and ensure resources are directed to the
regions, habitats and fisheries where they are
most needed.
Expand hunter-led conservation
This term, National delivered two herds of special
interest. This reflects that National believes that
hunters should play a greater role in managing
animal populations and protecting the places in
which they hunt.
A re-elected National Government will seek proposals
for additional herds of special interest, building on
the wapiti and sika models. The final selections will
be evidence-based and require strong local and
hunter support.
National will also replace the outdated Tahr Control
Plan 1993 with a modern management plan developed
alongside the tahr hunting community.

Protect recreational access
Access to public land, rivers, lakes and the coast
is fundamental to hunting and fishing. National
recognises this, this is why National launched an
Access Charter to ensure better access for recreational
hunting and fishing on public conservation land across
New Zealand.
A re-elected National will strengthen the Charter by
adding the Game Animal Council, Land Information
New Zealand and the Overseas Investment Office
as signatories.
We will change the current policy that generally
prevents recreational hunting on Crown land
managed by Land Information New Zealand.
Suitable Crown land that would ordinarily be
accessible to the public will be opened for hunting and
fishing under rules similar to those applying on public
conservation land. Existing arrangements for Crown
pastoral leases and other land that is not ordinarily
publicly accessible will remain unchanged.
National will also ensure existing recreational access
is protected when sensitive land is purchased by
overseas investors and improved where practical.
Growing hunting-related jobs and exports
Hunting supports the economy. guides, outfitters,
taxidermists, accommodation providers, tourism
operators and rural businesses throughout regional
New Zealand.
National will promote New Zealand’s premium
guided-hunting offer in key overseas markets and
simplify trophy-export permits, veterinary certification,
taxidermy requirements and customs processes.
National will also develop clearer rules for recreational
hunting, guided hunting, aerial hunting and commercial
wild animal recovery. These activities serve different
purposes and should be managed in ways that reduce
conflict and protect conservation, recreational and
economic outcomes.

Authorised by J de Joux, ps@national.org.nz

Other initiatives to ensure as many New Zealanders
can go hunting and fishing as possible
Investigate options for sustainable funding of national
hunter training programmes, alongside the Firearms
Safety Authority, to help deliver the training and
education of the next generation of hunters.
Direct Fish and Game regions to review their
existing regional boundaries to better align with
the Government’s
Resource Management Act and local government
reorganisation reforms, as well as to resolve existing
issues in cross-boundary catchment management.
Partner with DOC and community organisations to
maintain and enhance access to public conservation
huts and facilities.
Give hunters and fishers a voice by replacing an
existing Conservation Authority and Conservation
Board seat with a permanent representative from the
hunting and fishing sector.
Ensure that the Outdoor Access Commission’s
public access maps are considered as part of the
Government’s investment into a new planning and
environmental online management system.
Simplify the consenting system for shooting ranges
to more accurately reflect a risk-based approach
and implement a pre-existing right to operate where
there is no ability to complain if someone moves to
the nuisance.
Pilot a Government-backed biodiversity credit
to recognise the environmental benefits of
hunter-led conservation.

# Water Security Policy

Published by the New Zealand National Party as a PDF policy document. Source: <https://assets.national.org.nz/web/prod/Water%20Security%20Policy.pdf?v=1791602967>.
The text below is the verbatim text layer of the PDF extracted with `pdftotext` (reading order). Line breaks follow the
PDF; tables and multi-column layouts may read out of order in this section, so a second rendering that preserves the
page layout (`pdftotext -layout`) follows it. Nothing has been added, removed or paraphrased.

## Full text (reading order)

Building the Future:

Securing water and fertiliser
to back NZ farmers
Reliable access to water and fertiliser is critical to
on-farm productivity. National will remove roadblocks
to new water storage infrastructure and reduce our
exposure to volatile global fertiliser markets.
New Zealand’s farmers and growers are the best in
the world. When they do well, the whole country does
well. The primary sector produces 82 per cent of
New Zealand’s exports and that money pays for the
hospitals, schools and roads every community relies
on. When farming grows, wages lift and our towns
grow with it.
In much the same way as New Zealand ensures we
have security of fuel and energy, security of water
and fertiliser enables our farmers to produce food
and generate the exports that are currently worth
$65.2 billion to New Zealand’s economy.
When farmers and growers have reliable water, they
produce more, take on more staff and more money
flows into the local town, which means more jobs in
regional communities.
National have an ambitious agenda for growth and
the world wants what we produce. In three years, we
have signed trade deals with India and the United Arab
Emirates and completed an agreement with the Gulf
states, and brought our deal with the European Union
into force early. The job now is to produce more of it.
National back our farmers to get on with what they
do best.

Authorised by J de Joux, ps@national.org.nz

Water Security
Water is one of New Zealand’s greatest strategic
advantages. It underpins our food and fibre production,
supports regional jobs and earns the export income
that pays for hospitals, schools and roads.
We get more rainfall and renewable freshwater per
person than almost any other developed nation. Yet too
many regions still face water shortages. We have the
water. We just don’t store enough of it. New Zealand
captures and uses about two per cent of its available
water resources. We can and should do better.
In our first term, National made water storage easier to
build. We gave water infrastructure 35-year permits, cut
compliance costs for small dams, opened the Primary
Sector Growth Fund to feasibility studies, passed the
Fast-track Approvals Act and appointed New Zealand’s
first Associate Minister of Agriculture responsible for
water security.
National believes we should plan for water security
the same way we plan for fuel and energy. That means
storing water when it is plentiful and using it well when
it is scarce. It means knowing where water will be
needed and giving regions a clear path to build the
storage they need.

Get schemes built
A re-elected National Government will commit $300
million in concessional loans to support water storage
projects to be built. The Primary Sector Growth Fund
will continue to provide support for pre-construction
studies for productive water storage projects.
Water projects can spend years moving between
hydrology, engineering, environmental assessment,
land access, user commitments, consenting and
finance. National want to see water storage projects
get the necessary approvals and get built quicker.
Our promise of concessional loan support will help
bridge the gap.

Behind those five, the register will build a longer,
nationally prioritised pipeline. Further priority areas
identified include:
•

Bay of Plenty orchards

•

Central Otago and Waitaki fruit growing

•

Upper South Island: Marlborough and Nelson

•

Southern dryland areas, where stored water is
the difference between a normal season and
destocking.

A proportionate approach to on-farm water
storage and irrigation

Deliver New Zealand’s first long-term water
infrastructure pipeline

We value on-farm storage and want more of it, built
well. A routine farm pond is not a high-consequence
hydro dam and should not be regulated as if it were.

New Zealand has many promising water infrastructure
proposals, but there is no single national view of
existing storage, future demand, climate risk or project
readiness. Work is often commissioned one project at
a time; information is gathered to different standards
and specialist capability is lost between projects.

National will make it easier for farmers and growers to
build water storage on their own land, by developing
a National Standard for on-farm water storage under
the new planning system. This will allow on-farm water
storage infrastructure to be built without the need for
costly resource consents.

A national water infrastructure pipeline will allow
connected storage, distribution, managed aquifer
recharge, renewal and on-farm options to be
considered together. Projects will be compared on the
value created per unit of water and per Crown dollar,
climate resilience, environmental outcomes, regional
benefits, affordability and readiness to proceed.

National will also make it easier to get consents
by introducing a National Standard for Irrigation to
ensure irrigation systems are designed and operated
to recognised best practice, improving water-use
efficiency, reducing environmental risk and providing
farmers with a simpler, nationally consistent set of rules.

We will start by prioritising five key regions
•

Northland

•

Tairāwhiti

•

Hawke’s Bay

•

Wairarapa

•

Canterbury

Each of these regions depend heavily on reliable water
for high-value food and fibre production. Each faces
growing pressure from drought and climate variability.
And each region already has storage work underway,
so Crown investment can get schemes built sooner
rather than starting from scratch.
The national water storage register will identify the
project/s in each of these regions to be prioritised for
funding from the $300 million in concessional loans.

A re-elected National Government will:
•

Commit $300 million in concessional loans
to get water storage projects built.

•

The Primary Sector Growth Fund will continue
to provide grants for feasibility studies.

•

Deliver New Zealand’s first long-term water
infrastructure pipeline, in partnership with
farmers, growers, councils and iwi.

•

Publish the first National Rural and
Provincial Water Use Strategy in 2027,
backed by a national water storage register.

•

Introduce a National Standard for on-farm
and other lower-risk off-stream water
storage, and

•

Introduce a National Standard for Irrigation
to make consenting easier for farmers and
growers.

Fiscal impact

Strengthening supply partnerships

The water storage concessional loan scheme will
be structured as four $75m tranches of lending, with
the write down cost of this lending managed through
the existing Primary Sector Growth Fund. The annual
write down cost of this lending is expected to be $16.3
million per annum. Since these loans are expected to
be repaid within ten years, we do not anticipate an
impact on the Government’s capital allowance.

New Zealand imports around two-thirds of its urea,
with significant volumes sourced from the Gulf,
particularly Saudi Arabia. Recent conflict and disruption
in the Middle East have shown how quickly shipping
risks can flow through to global fertiliser prices and
availability. Other key nutrients, including phosphate
rock, potash and sulphur, are also exposed to
concentrated production, commodity cycles and
long transport routes.

Critical soil nutrients
Fertiliser is a critical nutrient input into New Zealand’s
food and fibre economy. Reliable access supports soil
fertility, farm productivity, export earnings and rural
communities. A serious supply disruption would be felt
well beyond the farm gate through lower production,
higher costs and weaker export returns.

National will treat fertiliser as a strategic priority in
trade, diplomatic and investment engagement. Using
the New Zealand–Singapore Agreement on Trade in
Essential Supplies as a blueprint, National will pursue
arrangements with key supplier countries focused on
reliable access, market diversification, early warning
and rapid government-to-government coordination.

New Zealand already plans for fuel and energy security,
but as events in the Middle East this year has shown,
we need to be planning for fertiliser security too.

A re-elected National Government will:

New Zealand uses over two million tonnes of fertiliser
to grow food each year. Our fertiliser production relies
on imported phosphate, which is then processed
on shore. This leaves our primary sector exposed
to international supply shocks. National will reduce
New Zealand’s exposure by supporting domestic
production, strengthening supply relationships, and
attracting investment in strategic infrastructure.
This is about ensuring a continued, stable supply of
fertiliser in the country. We will back measures to support
farmers to responsibly manage their nutrient use to
better support productive farming and the environment.

•

Negotiate fertiliser security agreements
with key supplier countries, using the
New Zealand–Singapore Agreement on Trade
in Essential Supplies as a model.

•

Establish a $10 million Critical Agri Inputs
Fund to co-invest in fertiliser production,
processing, storage and distribution projects
from the Primary Sector Growth Fund.

documents/policy-47-point-plan-small-bus.text:
# National’s plan to support Small Businesses

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/policies/47-point-plan-small-businesses> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## National’s plan to support Small Businesses

National knows the only way to create jobs and help Kiwis get ahead is to grow the economy, spend sensibly and get debt down, with no new taxes. Backing small businesses to succeed is a key part of how we make that happen.

Our small businesses are the backbone of our economy. National has their back.

From the local dairy to the mechanic, the family farm to the manufacturer, café or tourism operator, small businesses make New Zealand tick. They build our homes, produce our food, keep our towns busy and take Kiwi products to the world.

Our Investment Boost policy has been a game changer. Businesses can immediately deduct 20 per cent of the cost of eligible new productive assets, giving them a powerful incentive to invest in better equipment, technology and premises.

We have restored 90-day trials for employers of every size, given contractors greater certainty, and passed the Employment Leave Act to replace the Holidays Act with a simpler system. We are making it easier for businesses to get paid, expanding eInvoicing and opening banking to greater competition. We have replaced the RMA, reformed building rules and made it easier to use trusted overseas products.

But there is more to do. For too many owners, running a business still means evenings spent on paperwork, uncertainty before taking on another employee, months resolving a straightforward dispute, delays getting approvals, fees eating into every payment and opportunities overseas that are simply too difficult to pursue.

National’s plan changes that. We will make it easier for a small business to take the leap and become an employer. National will introduce a First Employee Support Package to help owners navigate requirements around payroll, employment agreements, tax, ACC and leave right from day one, and less paperwork for apprentices and seasonal workers.

## What we'll do

1

### Delivering a Tell Government Once service

built around the New Zealand Business Number and existing government systems including Inland Revenue, ACC, the Companies Office and relevant licensing bodies

2

### A fast track for straightforward disputes

within the Employment Relations Authority, for suitable minor employment disputes

3

### Reviewing the compulsory GST registration threshold

which has remained at $60,000 since 2009

4

### Rewriting priority health and safety codes

and guidance in plain English, with practical examples for small businesses

5

### Helping more small and medium Kiwi businesses succeed overseas

by backing the next 200 high-potential exporters with intensive support

6

### Making repeat seasonal hiring easier

with a standard recurring seasonal agreement and shorter renewal process

7

### Keeping Investment Boost

protecting the immediate 20 per cent deduction that backs businesses to invest, grow and hire.

## National’s 47-point plan to support Small Businesses

Read the complete policy as a PDF.

View full document

documents/policy-backing-auckland.md.text:
# Building the Future: Backing Auckland to succeed

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/policies/backing-auckland> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## Building the Future: Backing Auckland to succeed

National is excited for Auckland’s future and, if re-elected, will spend the next three years continuing to back our largest city to grow and prosper.

Auckland is New Zealand’s largest economic centre, home to more than 1.8 million people and contributing nearly 40 per cent of the country’s GDP. When Auckland succeeds, New Zealand succeeds. National is excited for Auckland’s future and, if re-elected, will spend the next three years continuing to back our largest city to grow and prosper.

We share Aucklanders’ vision for a city where families can get ahead, businesses can succeed, and communities can be proud of where they live. National has a strong record of backing Auckland, from the Waterview Tunnel and City Rail Link to the Auckland Regional Deal and major transport investments.

There is more to do. Auckland is still growing, and National’s focus is on building the infrastructure, services and opportunities the city needs for the future.

## What we'll do

1

### Abolish the blanket ban on minimum car parking requirements

2

### Allow councils to use minimum car parking requirements in suburban areas outside those identified for intensification (e.g. in city centres or around rapid transit stops).

## Transport

1

### Fund $1.75 billion to construct Mill Road Stage One and $100 million to route protect Stages Two and Three

progressing this critical new transport connection for South Auckland.

2

### Take the next steps on Auckland’s future harbour crossing

progressing the Detailed Business Case and the work needed to determine how this project can be funded and delivered.

3

### Complete the Eastern Busway through to Botany

giving East Auckland a faster and more reliable public transport connection.

4

### Progress North-West Rapid Transit

improving public transport along one of Auckland’s busiest and fastest-growing corridors.

5

### Progress CRL level-crossing removals

improving connections and safety across South and East Auckland and making the rail network safer and more reliable.

6

### Deliver the Auckland Deal

including a coordinated 30-year transport strategy so Auckland can plan ahead rather than constantly play catch-up.

7

### Explore options to speed up rapid transit projects

like the Botany to Airport Busway, through rescoping and cost saving measures.

## Law and order

1

### Deliver the Auckland Transport Police Team and make public transport safer

putting dedicated officers across buses, trains, ferries, stations and interchanges to protect passengers and staff.

2

### Keep Police visible and focused on the places and offenders causing the most harm

with a strong presence in neighbourhoods, town centres and other public spaces.

3

### Keep driving down burglary, theft and violent offending

with tougher consequences for serious and repeat offenders and a continued focus on reducing the number of victims.

## Frontline services

1

### Cancer patients in West Auckland can now receive more treatment closer to home

with infusion services opened at Waitākere Hospital and Te Whānau o Waipareira’s Whānau Centre in Henderson.

2

### Families in South and East Auckland once again have access to urgent care 24 hours a day

after round-the-clock services were restored in Counties Manukau.

3

### Progress the future South Auckland hospital at Drury

now that the 13 hectare Karaka Road site has been secured, so planning can continue for the services Auckland’s growing south will need.

4

### A new 30-bed spinal rehabilitation centre is being built at Manukau Health Park

backed by $128.5 million of investment.

5

### Auckland City Hospital is getting upgraded stroke and interventional radiology services

with new investment increasing capacity and replacing ageing equipment used in some of the most complex procedures.

6

### Cardiac services are being upgraded across the region

with catheter laboratory improvements planned or underway at Auckland City, Counties Manukau, North Shore and Starship.

7

### More care is being shifted closer to patients through primary care

with a new Auckland and Northland workforce hub supporting more than 400 GP clinics and training clinicians to provide more procedures outside hospital.

8

### Reduce waits and improve outcomes for Aucklanders,

continuing to deliver National’s elective boost with more hip, knee and cataract surgeries, alongside a continued focus on emergency care, specialist assessments and childhood immunisation.

9

### Catch cancer earlier and get more medicines to Aucklanders

with a further $604 million for Pharmac, free bowel screening from age 50, free breast screening extended to 74, free cervical screening for women aged 25 to 69, and new prostate and lung cancer screening pilots.

## Education

1

### Deliver the remaining 499 funded classrooms

completing the 203 already under construction and getting the next 296 underway.

2

### Progress Drury Specialist School towards opening in Term 1, 2028

delivering six classrooms for up to 54 students with high and complex needs.

3

### Secure the Drury East primary-school site

protecting the land needed for future school capacity as southern Auckland grows.

4

### Keep lifting attendance

so more Auckland children are in the classroom regularly and getting the benefit of every school day.

5

### Keep improving achievement

with a focus on making sure more students leave school with the qualifications they need for work, training or further study.

# Giving more Kiwis access to 5% first home deposits

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/policies/backing-first-home-buyers> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## Giving more Kiwis access to 5% first home deposits

Owning a home is a central part of the Kiwi dream.

Owning a home is a central part of the Kiwi dream. Home ownership provides families with stability, financial security and a stronger stake in their communities. It is also part of what makes New Zealand an attractive place for ambitious young people to build a career, raise a family and invest in their future. National believes that New Zealand should be a country where if you work hard, you should be able to get ahead.

A re-elected National Government will support more New Zealanders to achieve the Kiwi dream of owning their own home by widening access to 5 per cent deposits under the Government’s First Home Loan scheme, making it easier to get a deposit for a house.

## What we'll do

1

### Widen access to 5 per cent deposit home loans

by extending the First Home Loan income cap to $300,000.

2

### Apply the $300,000 income cap to all applicants

a change from the current criteria of the First Home Loan scheme where the income cap for individual buyers with no dependents is $95,000 and multiple buyers combined or individual buyers with dependents is $150,000.

## What National’s changes means for first home buyers

The current income limits under the First Home Loan scheme increasingly exclude many working New Zealanders who are capable of servicing a mortgage but still struggle to save a 20 per cent deposit as they juggle everyday costs like rent, food and childcare.

The First Home Loan scheme reduces the size of the deposit required to purchase a home. National’s changes mean that all first home buyers earning up to $300,000 will be able to access the scheme, no matter whether they are single without dependents or a couple.

# Backing Waikato: Investing in growth

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/policies/backing-waikato> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## Backing Waikato: Investing in growth

National is backing that growth with the infrastructure Waikato needs for the future.

Waikato is New Zealand’s productive heartland.

It is where much of our food is grown, our energy is generated, our exports are made and our freight moves through. Hamilton and the surrounding towns are growing quickly, while rural and coastal communities depend on strong connections and reliable services.

National is backing that growth with the infrastructure Waikato needs for the future.

That investment is anchored by two major projects. National is extending the Waikato Expressway from Cambridge to Piarere and building the new Waikato Medical School in Hamilton, which will provide 120 additional medical training places each year from 2028. But the investment goes much further. We are progressing Hamilton Southern Links, expanding Hamilton Airport, strengthening transport resilience in the Coromandel, adding classrooms and specialist education capacity, increasing health capacity, supporting more housing, and backing major productive infrastructure across the region.

We also invested a record $1.9 billion into the Waikato’s roads through the 2024-27 National Land Transport Fund, ensuring the region’s roads are up to standard. Construction has also begun on replacing the SH25 Pepe Stream bridge, the SH25 Ramarama Stream Bridge and the SH27 Ohinekaua Stream bridge – improving the resilience of the wider Waikato state highway network and keeping local communities, freight and emergency services moving.

We are building the housing our most vulnerable in the Waikato needs, with more than 900 additional social houses being delivered in the Waikato under National.

We are also working to make Waikato communities safer. Ram raids have fallen sharply from their peak, theft and robbery are down, Police foot patrols have more than doubled, and tougher laws are giving Police stronger tools to target gangs and repeat offenders.

There is more to do. National will keep building the infrastructure Waikato needs to grow, while making sure families, businesses and communities can share in the benefits..

## What we'll do

1

### Back Waikato’s productive economy

By supporting farming, manufacturing, energy, mining and exports.

2

### Build the infrastructure Waikato needs to grow

By improving the roads and connections that move people, freight and goods around the region and to market.

3

### Support fast-growing communities

Making sure housing, schools, health services and essential infrastructure keep pace.

4

### Strengthen services closer to home

Particularly for rural and regional communities.

5

### Keep Police visible and communities safe

With a continued focus on serious, repeat and retail offending.

# Back Pocket Boost for Graduates

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/policies/boost-for-graduates> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## Back Pocket Boost for Graduates

National’s Back Pocket Boost for Graduates will reward young graduates who choose to stay in New Zealand

A re-elected National Government will let Kiwis with student loans keep more of what they earn, while toughening up on those who leave the country before paying back their loan. National will reduce the compulsory student loan repayment rate from 12 per cent to 10 per cent from 1 April 2027 and introduce tougher measures to recover student loan debt from people who move overseas.

Encouraging young people to stay in New Zealand to build a career, start a business, raise a family and make a contribution to the community and economy is critical to National’s plan to fix the basics and build the future.

## What we'll do

1

### Reduce the compulsory student loan repayment rate for domestic borrowers from 12 per cent to 10 per cent from 1 April 2027.

This means that: • An early career accountant earning $75,000 per year will keep an additional $39 each fortnight, or around $1,000 a year. • An early career engineer earning $80,000 per year will keep an additional $43 each fortnight, or around $1,100 a year. • A junior doctor earning $100,000 per year will keep an additional $58 each fortnight, or around $1,500 a year.

2

### Introduce tougher measures to recover student loan debt from people who move overseas

New financial penalties: 1 per cent added to annual interest on overseas-based borrower balances, taking it to 6.6 per cent, with tiered penalties for sustained default, on top of existing late payment interest. Restricted KiwiSaver withdrawals, so people who move overseas permanently must clear their student loan before accessing KiwiSaver. Tighter arrest settings, so arrest warrants can be sought for serious, sustained default without needing to prove a borrower knowingly refused to pay.

# National to make it easier to build the future

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/policies/build-the-future> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## National to make it easier to build the future

A more efficient building consent system

National will make it easier to build shops, offices and other commercial buildings by removing unnecessary delays and costs in the building consent system.

Under National, qualified engineers will be able to sign off certain building work without needing a council inspection. National will also designate a specialist Building Consent Authority to engage through a single, nationally consistent pathway for consents.

## What we'll do

1

### Less red tape for commercial projects

allowing qualified engineers to sign off building work, without the need for a council inspection by formalising the role of producer statements in the Building Act.

2

### A dedicated Building Consent Authority for large commercial buildings

will provide major projects with a single clear, nationally consistent pathway with the right specialist expertise.

3

### Freeing up councils to focus on housing

Complex projects will no longer need to depend on a local council happening to have specialist staff available. It will also free up councils to focus more on standard and residential consents to support more Kiwis to build or renovate their home.

4

### Getting projects moving faster

For retailers, developers, and businesses, it means less time stuck in consenting and more certainty to invest, expand and create jobs. For families and communities, it means new shops, workplaces, and local amenities can be built sooner and at lower cost.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Producer statements are professional documents used to support building consent applications and code compliance certification.

MBIE describes a producer statement as a professional opinion based on specialist expertise. They are commonly used where building work involves technical areas such as structural engineering, fire design, geotechnical work, or proprietary systems.

Producer statements help Building Consent Authorities, or BCAs, decide whether there are reasonable grounds to issue a building consent or code compliance certificate. They provide councils with assurance from qualified professionals and can reduce the need for councils to duplicate specialist checks.

There are four main types of producer statements: PS1 – Design: confirms aspects of the design. PS2 – Design Review: confirms an independent review of aspects of the design. PS3 – Construction: often used by installers of proprietary systems. PS4 – Construction Review: confirms review of construction work.

Producer statements are already well-established and widely used across the building sector. However, they do not currently have a formal statutory status under the Building Act 2004.

This means councils can choose how much weight to give a producer statement and may still carry out their own checks, even where specialist professionals have already reviewed the work.

The current system therefore supports the use of producer statements but does not provide a clear or consistent framework for relying on them. This can create duplication, delay and uncertainty, particularly for large or complex building projects where specialist engineers are already designing, reviewing and monitoring key parts of the work.

Developers can choose to use the dedicated BCA’s service or continue with their local BCA as usual.

For in-scope projects accepted by the dedicated BCA, other BCAs are not expected to process these applications but may be contacted for information or for coordinating services.

The new dedicated commercial BCA will be modelled off the building consent service for supermarket developments announced last year. A preferred provider will be selected following a closed competitive sourcing process.

Buildings considered as category Commercial 3 under the National Building Consent Authority Competency Assessment System will be in-scope of the new BCA. Category 3 covers large or complex commercial buildings, including high-rise or high-occupancy structures, generally over 4 storeys or more and which can have more than 500 occupants.

documents/policy-consent-laws.md.text:
# Modernise Sexual Consent Laws

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/policies/consent-laws> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## Modernise Sexual Consent Laws

National will continue to build the future where every New Zealander feels safe.

National is focused on fixing the basics in law and order, and modernising our consent laws is an important part of that. Unlike other jurisdictions we normally compare ourselves with, New Zealand law does not define what consent is. Rather, the Crimes Act provides a non-exhaustive list of what consent is not. If re-elected, National will change the law to specify that consent must be actively given, meaning there must be a 'yes' rather than the absence of a 'no.' That 'yes' can be communicated by words or actions.

## What we'll do

1

### Change the law to specify that consent must be actively given

meaning there must be a "yes" rather than the absence of a "no". Silence is not consent, and consent given once is not consent forever.

2

### Ensure the prosecution will still need to prove beyond reasonable doubt that consent wasn't given

and that the defendant didn't believe on reasonable grounds that it was.

3

### This builds on our promise to ban good character discounts at sentencing for all sexual offending

and our work in government to give sexual violence victims the power to determine whether their perpetrators receive permanent name suppression, and making stalking illegal and a jailable offence.

The change would align the law with what we've been telling our kids for a long time: that you need positive consent before sex, each and every time, rather than presuming it. It also resets social expectations, so that sex is understood as something both people actively choose. Explaining what consent is, not just what it isn't, helps judges and juries.

National will continue to build the future where every New Zealander feels safe, in their communities, in their relationships, and in their own homes.

# National sets out plan to double exports by 2034

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/policies/double-exports> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## National sets out plan to double exports by 2034

New Zealand’s farmers and growers are the best in the world. When they do well, the whole country does well.

New Zealand’s farmers and growers are the best in the world. When they do well, the whole country does well.

Food and fibre earns around four in every five dollars of our goods exports and supports about 360,000 jobs, most of them in our regions. That export income pays for the hospitals, schools and roads in every New Zealand community. When farming grows, it delivers more jobs, wages lift and the regions across the country thrive.

National’s ambition is clear: to make New Zealand the world’s leading producer of high-value, premium and sustainable food and fibre. The plan is working, but the job is not done. National is focused on the key drivers that make a difference to growth: more markets, less risk for farmers; getting more from our land and more value from every kilo; and secure and enabling foundations.

WHAT WE'LL DO

## Deliver 19 national standards for farming

1

### Farm Plans

A national standard for farm plans will give farmers one practical, consistent, risk-based way to identify and manage environmental risks on their land. This will ensure approaches to farm plans don’t differ wildly from council to council.

2

### Vegetable growing

A national standard for vegetable growing, including making it a permitted activity when certain conditions are met, will give growers certainty to keep producing the fresh food that feeds our country.

3

### On-farm water storage

We value on-farm storage and want more of it, built well. A national standard will make it easier to build low-risk water storage, like ponds and small dams, to help farmers and growers get through dry periods.

4

### Gravel extraction

Responsible gravel extraction can reduce the flood risk and provide a local source of aggregate. A national standard will allow farmers to remove gravel from rivers under clear, consistent conditions that protect ecosystem health.

5

### Drain maintenance

Consents can be required for certain types of on-farm drain maintenance, adding cost and complexity. A national standard for drain maintenance will let farmers clear and maintain their existing drains without navigating confusing, fragmented rules.

6

### Effluent management

A national standard for effluent management will set clear nationwide requirements for the storage and application of farm effluent. This will ensure there are consistent best practice rules so farmers can realise on-farm benefits while still protecting the environment.

7

### Fertiliser application

A national standard for fertiliser application will set consistent rules for using fertiliser in a way that supports productivity while protecting waterways.

8

### Farm quarries

Small-scale on-farm quarries provide gravel, sand, and rock required to build and maintain important infrastructure. A national standard for farm quarries will let farmers extract rock and aggregate from their own land without consenting processes rendering this uneconomic.

9

### Wetlands

Wetland rules are confusing and have led to significant amounts of uncertainty and litigation in the past. A national standard for wetlands will make it simpler for farmers, removing the red tape in the way of doing the right thing.

10

### On-farm solar

We will make small-scale on-farm ground-mounted solar, as well as rooftop solar, permitted activities with standard rules to manage genuine effects and sensible safeguards to protect land that is environmentally significant.

11

### Micro-hydro

A national standard for small run-of-river micro-hydro will help farmers generate the power they need to run their businesses, using the water they already have on their property.

12

### Energy storage

A national standard for energy storage will let farmers install batteries and other storage that support on-farm energy generation and resilience.

13

### Irrigation

A national standard for Irrigation will make consenting easier for farmers and growers, providing them with a set of nationally consistent rules so that irrigation systems are designed and operated in accordance with recognised best practice, improving efficiency and environmental protection.

14

### Small-scale seasonal-worker accommodation

A national standard for small-scale seasonal-worker accommodation, modelled off our successful granny-flats standards, will make it easier for farmers and growers to house the workers they need at peak times.

15

### Farm tracks

A national standard for farm tracks will let farmers build and maintain access tracks, with sensible controls on erosion and sediment.

16

### Agricultural aviation

A national standard for agricultural aviation will provide consistent rules for airstrips, aerial topdressing and spraying, which Kiwis rely on for both farming and conservation efforts.

17

### Culverts

A national standard for culverts will set clear requirements for installing and replacing basic culverts so stock and vehicles can cross waterways safely, without the costly red-tape.

18

### Offal holes

A national standard for offal holes will give farmers clear, consistent rules for disposing of dead stock and offal on farm without the need for a consent.

19

### Managing contaminated soils

A re-worked national standard for managing contaminated soils will give farmers a consistent, pragmatic approach to dealing with legacy contamination on their property while still ensuring the land is safe to use.

# Teaching the basics brilliantly

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/policies/education-teaching-the-basics-brilliantly> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## Teaching the basics brilliantly

National’s vision is a world-leading education system that raises achievement and gives every young New Zealander the opportunity to succeed.

Every child deserves an education that opens doors. The knowledge to understand the world, the skills to contribute to it, and the confidence to build a successful future.

National’s vision is a world-leading education system that raises achievement and gives every young New Zealander the opportunity to succeed.

A child’s background, postcode, or learning needs should never set the limit on what they can achieve. We believe in high expectations for every child, excellent teaching in every classroom, and additional support when needed.

A great education is the foundation of opportunity for individuals and of stronger economic growth and prosperity for New Zealand. That starts in the early years, with children developing the language, skills and confidence they need for school.

It continues through a clear, knowledge-rich curriculum, effective teaching, regular assessment, and warm, dry classrooms.

It means parents knowing how their child is progressing, teachers having the training and resources to teach well, and young people leaving school with credible qualifications and pathways into further study, training and employment.

Over the past three years, National has begun a transformation of education. We have restored a focus on the basics and backed teachers with the tools to deliver them.

Encouraging results are beginning to emerge. Our next term will build on that foundation: helping children arrive at school Set Up for Success and giving them More Time Learning once they get there.

## What we'll do

1

### Introduce a School Start Check for every child before they start school

2

### Establish clearer developmental milestones throughout early childhood education and report progress to parents

3

### Connect children who need additional support with the expanded Early Intervention Service

4

### Introduce no screens or individual device use in early childhood education

5

### Set tight limits on screen and individual-device use in Years 1-3, with age-appropriate limits for older primary students

6

### Require the writing component of twice-yearly primary assessments to be completed on paper

7

### Require students to stay at school until they complete Year 11 or turn 16, whichever is later

8

### Set consistent school start and finish dates to make the school calendar more predictable for families

9

### Replacing NCEA, beginning in 2028, with new qualifications backed by a clear senior secondary curriculum and stronger subject-based assessment

10

### Learning Support Coordinators for all schools with Year 1–8 students from 2028

11

### Additional teacher-aide hours and training to support children with behavioural, emotional and neurodiverse needs – building to two million extra hours every year from 2028

12

### Deliver more warm, dry classrooms and better value for school property investment.

# Affordable power Kiwis can rely on

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/policies/electrify-nz-2> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## Affordable power Kiwis can rely on

delivering more supply, more competition, and more choice for households and businesses, to help make power more affordable.

Delivering secure, affordable energy is critical to National’s plan to grow the economy and support New Zealanders with the cost of living. That’s why over this term National has undertaken a series of significant actions designed to enable new renewable generation, supported by more backup supply, and pro-competition rules that ensure the market works for everyone.

As a result, wholesale electricity prices have fallen significantly, and the country now has the strongest, most secure pipeline of new renewable generation in a generation – with new wind farms, solar farms, geothermal and battery projects. According to the Electricity Authority, more renewable generation has now been built in the last three years than the previous eight.

For households, that means there now exists a credible path to more affordable electricity prices over time. For businesses, lower wholesale electricity prices also mean manufacturers and exporters can remain internationally competitive, supporting economic.

A re-elected National Government will build on our success this term with Electrify NZ 2.0, a nine-point plan delivering more supply, more competition, and more choice for households and businesses, to help make power more affordable.

## What we'll do

1

### Unlock new energy development zones

By letting developers, major energy users, and investors build and own new transmission, and recover their costs from the parties who use the lines.

2

### Make connections faster and cheaper

By giving every household, builder, and business the right to choose an accredited contractor for the connection work they’re paying for, not the one their network hands them.

3

### Let Kiwis sell their power to the best buyer

Giving every household and business with solar or a battery the right to sell the power they export to any power company, not just the one they buy from.

4

### Addressing the dry year problem

By levelling the playing field for backup power. National will use transparency, a standardised backup power contract, and regular auctions to open the closed backup market and draw in the competition and investment that keeps the lights on through dry periods.

5

### Tackle lines charges

Through a targeted review of Part 4 of the Commerce Act and put an end to slow solar approvals by requiring distribution businesses to sign off residential and small business connections within two working days.

6

### Make affordability a core objective for the Electricity Authority

By writing it into law, so the cost of power for households and businesses carries equal weight with competition, reliability, and efficiency in every decision the regulator makes.

7

### Cut more red tape holding back renewables at every scale

From national rules letting Kiwis install solar, micro-hydro, and batteries on their own property without a consent, to implementing the RMA replacement so wind, solar, and hydro get built fast as standard, not the exception.

8

### Launch the Home Energy Fund

Giving Kiwis low-interest, long-term loans to invest in their own power and cut their own bills.

9

### Require AI data centres to bring new, firmed power

So new digital investment adds to the grid and creates jobs instead of pushing up prices for families and businesses.

# National’s plan for healthy fisheries

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/policies/fisheries> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## National’s plan for healthy fisheries

to protect the things Kiwis care about and continue our plan to grow the economy, spend sensibly and get debt down, with no new taxes.

The health of our ocean matters to every New Zealander. It is part of who we are, provides us food, recreation, well-being, and a place for families and communities to connect.

We must strike the balance between environmental, recreational, customary and commercial interests and look after the long-term health of the whole ocean. We need to understand the asset, manage it well, and hand it on to future generations in better condition than we found it.

We want fish stocks managed at healthy and abundant levels, not simply kept above minimum sustainability limits. Our decisions will be guided by the best available science, data and evidence, while upholding property rights and the Crown's Treaty settlement obligations. Commercial and recreational interests must be balanced in a way that protects this asset for those who come after us.

Fishing

## What we'll do

1

### Establish a new marine reserve off Waiheke Island and further expand the size of Goat Island/Te Hāwere-a-Maki Marine Reserve

2

# Plan to fix Fire and Emergency New Zealand

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/policies/fix-fire-and-emergency> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## Plan to fix Fire and Emergency New Zealand

By ensuring firefighters have reliable trucks, proper training, practical support, and an organisation accountable for delivering the tools they need to do their job.

More than 14,000 firefighters, including volunteers, paid staff, and frontline enablers, work hard every day to keep our communities safe. They deserve more than our thanks; they deserve an organisation that is as reliable and prepared as they are.

Nine years after Fire and Emergency New Zealand was created, frontline firefighters still face equipment and training shortages. National backs our firefighters and knows things can be much better. National will reset Fire and Emergency New Zealand by backing firefighters and restoring accountability.

## What we'll do

1

### Restore accountability and reset Fire and Emergency New Zealand

By making Fire and Emergency New Zealand directly accountable to the Minister for Emergency Management and Recovery, removing unnecessary bureaucracy and keeping operational decisions with fire and emergency professionals. A turnaround plan will also be developed and implemented, with all reforms funded within existing baselines.

2

### Support volunteer firefighters

by requiring Fire and Emergency New Zealand to provide private insurance covering event based mental injury and gradual process injuries for operational volunteers, giving volunteers and their families greater support and financial security.

3

### Back the frontline with the tools they need to do their job

By delivering the fire appliances firefighters need, establishing a long-term fleet replacement programme, restoring live fire training, reducing unnecessary red tape, and ensuring frontline operational capability comes first.

# More grocery competition

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/policies/grocery-competition> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## More grocery competition

So Kiwis get a fairer deal at the checkout

National will pursue a separation of New World and PAK’nSAVE so they compete harder against each other for shoppers with better pricing, specials and range. Kiwis deserve a fair deal at the checkout, while local supermarket owner-operators and suppliers deserve to be able to compete harder and have more options to grow their business.

National believes in competitive enterprise and the evidence shows supermarket competition is too weak in New Zealand, compared to most similar sized countries which have at least three large supermarket chains. Separating New World and PAK’nSAVE would mean that, together with Woolworths, New Zealand would have three large supermarket chains and that could save shoppers an average of $560 a year.

National is not pursuing structural separation in any other sector. There is a very high bar for this intervention, which is why the Commerce Commission will need to confirm that is stacks up for shoppers. If it does, National will pursue it.

## Shoppers

### New Zealanders work hard for their money and deserve a fair deal at the checkout. But right now, they’re paying more than they should because supermarket competition is too weak.

### More competition means supermarkets have to work harder for every customer who walks through the door, through better pricing, special and range.

### A better deal for Kiwi shoppers is the whole point of this policy, so if the Commerce Commission confirms that a separation stacks up, we will pursue it. If it doesn’t, we won’t.

## Owner-operators

### Local supermarket owner-operators are hardworking people who employ local staff, invest in their communities and often run very good businesses.

### We back them to keep doing what they’re doing. A separation won’t change much for them, except they’ll be able to be more competitive than they currently are.

### No owner of a PAK’nSAVE, New World or Four Square will be forced to sell or re-brand. They would retain ownership of their businesses, continue to operate under their existing brand, and remain part of a larger cooperative group.

## Suppliers

### Competition matters for suppliers too. Local growers and producers deserve a grocery market where supermarkets compete for their product, not one where they feel they have to take what they are offered.

### More competition means suppliers have more options about where to supply and more leverage to secure better terms from supermarkets wanting to secure and keep a supplier’s product.

### A more competitive supermarket sector also gives smaller and emerging suppliers a better chance of getting on shelves and reaching New Zealanders.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Scale creates efficiencies – efficient buying, technology, logistics and distribution can reduce costs. The question is who gets the benefit. We want a market where competition forces supermarkets to pass efficiencies through to shoppers. Right now, the evidence suggests that is not happening. The cost-benefit analysis explicitly considered restructuring costs, duplicated distribution and overhead functions, and changes to supply-chain costs – it showed the benefits outweighed the costs. The Commerce Commission will be required to test this to confirm. Compared to countries of a similar size, New Zealand’s grocery market is unusual. Most developed countries of a similar size have at least three major grocery competitors, or equivalent competitive pressure from large discounters and other formats. See next Q+A.

New Zealand’s grocery market is unusual internationally. Most developed countries of a similar size have at least three major grocery competitors, or equivalent competitive pressure from large discounters and other formats.

Examples include: • Denmark: 4 large traditional supermarket groups plus Lidl. • Norway: 3 large traditional supermarket groups plus a regional supermarket group. • Ireland: 3 large traditional supermarket groups plus Aldi and Lidl. • Iceland: 3 large supermarket groups plus Costco. • Finland: 2 large traditional groups plus a global hard discounter and other competing formats.

The Commerce Commission has also said three major national supermarket networks would be significantly more competitive than two and that this is achievable in New Zealand. New Zealand also has relatively few supermarkets for its population. Commerce Commission analysis found New Zealand has 12.8 supermarkets per 100,000 people, compared with an OECD average of 16.6. Norway, with a population similar to New Zealand, has almost twice as many supermarkets per person.

There are genuine implementation risks. Distribution, logistics, supply arrangements and technology systems all matter. That is precisely why National is not simply ordering Foodstuffs to split. The Commerce Commission will have to develop and assess a detailed implementation proposal and consider:

• Commercial viability • Supply-chain resilience • Duplication and efficiency costs • Impacts on suppliers and owner-operators • Rural and regional access • Implementation costs and practical feasibility.

This does not apply to any other sector. This is a targeted, grocery-specific action which is deliberately being put through a grocery specific legislation. The current structure of New Zealand’s grocery market makes it very difficult for new players wanting to invest in and enter the market.

Market intervention of this scale is not something we considered lightly, and it is only something we are pursuing with the supermarkets, not any other sector. The evidence is clear that the grocery market is not working for consumers, the supermarket owner-operators, or the suppliers of the major supermarkets. National believes in competitive enterprise, and the current structure of the market means there is weak competition.

The Government commissioned the independent work because we wanted to understand whether structural change could materially improve competition. That work produced a serious case for pursuing separation of Foodstuffs. Given the significance of the proposal, National believes the right course is to put it before New Zealand and seek an explicit mandate. Even with that mandate, separation would not happen automatically. It would remain subject to the Commerce Commission independently concluding that a practical restructure would enhance competition and leave consumers better off.

Through the work Nicola has done, it became clear that structural separation should be pursued. That is a very significant intervention and not one that we had a mandate for, so National is seeking that mandate at this year’s election.

The oil and gas ban was a decision made without evidence, by politicians, for political purposes. This is an action where the final decision will be made by independent experts, where a lot of evidence has already been gathered that separation would benefit consumers.

The CBA tested restructuring Foodstuffs alone and both Foodstuffs and Woolworths, and found restructuring Foodstuffs alone would deliver greater benefits for shoppers.

Foodstuffs is different because it already has separate, established banners. Under this option, owner-operators would keep their stores and their brands. The change is about creating genuinely independent competing supermarket groups from the existing New World/Four Square and PAK’nSAVE businesses.

Doing the same to Woolworths would be much more intrusive. It would require individual Woolworths stores to be sold or transferred to create a separate competitor and brand, raising much greater property-rights and implementation issues. And Woolworths shoppers still benefit from stronger competition.

As the CBA puts it: “Woolworths prices will go down if/when Foodstuffs is restructured - they are not immune from the ensuing price war.” The objective is not to break up businesses for the sake of it. It is to create the strongest additional competition with the least unnecessary disruption.

# National backs South Island growth

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/policies/hunters-and-anglers> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## National backs South Island growth

The South Island needs infrastructure that keeps communities connected and supports future growth.

The South Island is now a powerhouse of the New Zealand economy – producing the food, fibre, energy, technology and visitor experiences the country needs and the world flocks to buy. In total, the South Island’s economy is worth almost $100 billion a year, or around 22 per cent of the New Zealand economy, and its ports carry around a third of New Zealand’s goods exports.

A re-elected National Government will build the transport and regional connections the South Island needs to move people, goods and visitors reliably. Grow Southern exports across agriculture, tourism, and mining and resources. Secure the energy new industrial investment needs; and strengthen the frontline health, education, and law and order services growing communities rely on.

## Infrastructure

1

### National will Invest $50 million in the shared road and rail connections for the Rolleston intermodal freight hub

2

### Ensure that congestion reducing Gondola solutions in Queenstown can access existing public transport funding in the NLTF

3

### Commit $25m to four-lane the remaining portion past Hansen Road down to the Five Mile roundabout in Queenstown

4

### Use the next Government Policy Statement to improve the network’s most critical links, including South Island state highway bridge replacements.

## Agriculture

1

### National will complete and implement the replacement of the RMA, giving farmers and growers certainty to invest

2

### Implement new Crown pastoral land settings so high-country farmers can invest and diversify with confidence.

## Tourism

1

2

### Introduce access charging for international visitors at Aoraki / Mt Cook and Milford Sounds, prioritising reinvestment in local conservation and tourism infrastructure

3

### Implement new conservation concession timeframes and publish regional performance.

## Mining and resources

1

### National will develop a new Government Policy Statement on Mining and Extraction under the Fast Track Approvals Act

2

### Develop a National Standard for gravel extraction from rivers, supporting aggregate supply and flood management

3

### Develop a National Standard for on-farm quarries, cutting consenting costs for farmers.

## Energy

1

### National will complete and implement the replacement of the RMA, with more enabling rules for wind, solar and hydro development

2

### Require new data centre projects to be accompanied by new, firmed generation, protecting households and businesses from higher power prices.

## Health & Education

1

### National will finish fitting out Tower Three at Christchurch Hospital, delivering 96 additional beds for patients

2

### Deliver the remaining funded teaching spaces, nearly 100 more classrooms across the South Island

3

### Complete the redevelopment programme underway across 14 South Island schools.

## Law and order

1

### National will deliver a new Police station for Greymouth through Budget 2026

2

### Complete Phase 1 of the Christchurch Men’s Prison redevelopment, operational by mid-2030.

## Building the South Island’s Future

The South Island has strong renewable resources and some of New Zealand’s best opportunities for new industrial investment. Growth is only worth having if it comes with the services growing communities rely on.

That is why National is focused on delivering the infrastructure needed to keep communities connected, support growth and unlock the South Island’s potential.

# Hunting and Fishing

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/policies/hunting-and-fishing> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## Hunting and Fishing

Hunting and fishing are part of the Kiwi way of life.

Hunting and fishing are part of the Kiwi way of life. They put food on the table, bring families and communities together, support regional jobs and tourism, and connect New Zealanders with the outdoors.

A re-elected National Government will strengthen hunter-led conservation, protect access to the outdoors, and better recognise the value of hunting and fishing to New Zealand.

## What we'll do

1

### Recognise valued introduced species in law

Establish a coordinated wild animal management framework and formally recognise valued introduced species in law. This will include introduced species that provide recreational, economic, environmental or cultural value to New Zealanders. They will not be treated as pests by default simply because they were introduced.

2

### Strengthen the Game Animal Council and modernise Fish & Game

Strengthen the Game Animal Council as the statutory manager of valued game animals, with a clearer role in managing herds of special interest and supporting practical hunter-led conservation. National will also pass legislation to modernise Fish & Game New Zealand. The reforms will simplify administration, strengthen accountability to licence holders and ensure resources are directed to the regions, habitats and fisheries where they are most needed.

3

### Expand Hunter-Led Conservation

Seek proposals for additional herds of special interest, building on the wapiti and sika models. The final selections will be evidence-based and require strong local and hunter support. National will also replace the outdated Tahr Control Plan 1993 with a modern management plan developed alongside the tahr hunting community.

4

### Protect Recreational Access and Support Regional Growth

Strengthen the Charter by adding the Game Animal Council, Land Information New Zealand and the Overseas Investment Office as signatories. We will change the current policy that generally prevents recreational hunting on Crown land managed by Land Information New Zealand. Suitable Crown land that would ordinarily be accessible to the public will be opened for hunting and fishing under rules similar to those applying on public conservation land. National will also ensure existing recreational access is protected when sensitive land is purchased by overseas investors and improved where practical.

5

### Growing hunting-related jobs and exports

Promote New Zealand’s premium guided-hunting offer in key overseas markets and simplify trophy-export permits, veterinary certification, taxidermy requirements and customs processes. National will also develop clearer rules for recreational hunting, guided hunting, aerial hunting and commercial wild animal recovery. These activities serve different purposes and should be managed in ways that reduce conflict and protect conservation, recreational and economic outcomes.

# International Visitor Levy reset to keep taxes low

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/policies/international-visitor-levy> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## International Visitor Levy reset to keep taxes low

We’re helping regions invest in the services they need to keep up with tourism growth

Tourism is our second-largest export earner and supports around one in nine jobs. National believes that growth should be managed responsibly, so regions that experience the benefits of New Zealand’s tourism industry aren’t also left to carry all of the costs. To support a vibrant tourism industry capable of maintaining its social licence, a re-elected National Government will reset funding from the International Visitor Levy (IVL), so councils see a direct and growing financial return from the visitors they host, without a new bed tax.

## What we'll do

1

### Direct more International Visitor Levy funding to conservation

by providing $100 million per annum to the Department of Conservation to keep investing in the conservation estate that underpins New Zealand's visitor experience.

2

### Create a Tourism Priorities Fund

by ring-fencing $50 million per annum to support tourism growth and resilience, including international marketing, visitor infrastructure in high-growth regions, event attraction, tourism data, and the tourism workforce.

3

### Regional funding for councils

by distributing all remaining IVL revenue to councils, based on their share of international visitor guest nights.

4

### Back the regions that host our visitors

by providing councils with funding that can be used for conservation and tourism purposes, including freedom-camping enforcement, public toilets and waste management, tourism promotion, event attraction, visitor infrastructure, and traffic and parking management.

5

### Provide certainty for tourism growth

by committing that there will be no increase in the International Visitor Levy for at least the next three years, while continuing to support sustainable tourism growth.

# Enhancing KiwiSaver for Everyone

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/policies/kiwisaver> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## Enhancing KiwiSaver for Everyone

Retire with more under our proposed KiwiSaver changes

Strengthening New Zealanders' financial security is central to our plan to fix the basics and build the future. At the heart of that plan are hardworking New Zealanders and their families, who deserve to get ahead when they work hard and make responsible choices for their future.

That's why we are making KiwiSaver compulsory for all workers, kickstarting every child's savings at birth, backing parents on leave, and ensuring older workers don't face an effective pay cut at 65.

See how National's plan grows your retirement savings — try the calculator to estimate your projected balance under our enhanced KiwiSaver.

National's KiwiSaver Calculator

## Our Plan for Kiwi Families

1

### Making every New Zealander a KiwiSaver

From 1 July 2028, National will make contributions to KiwiSaver (or an equivalent scheme) compulsory for all workers. Contributions will be made at the prevailing default rate as part of the agreed glidepath, lifting combined default contributions to 12% by 2032. Ensuring every New Zealander is financially prepared for retirement is a top priority.

2

### $1,500 Baby Boost & Auto-Enrolment at Birth

From 1 July 2027, National will enrolment in KiwiSaver at birth will be automatic, and matched with a $1,500 Baby Boost payment to kickstart their retirement savings, which will benefit from decades of compounding returns. At the heart of National is a belief in New Zealand as a property-owning democracy, where every Kiwi has a real stake in the future of our economy. Making that a practical, financial reality for every child growing up in New Zealand today should be a priority.

3

### Paid Parental Leave Top-Up

From 1 July 2027, National will provide a KiwiSaver contribution to people on paid parental leave even if the person is not contributing themselves. This contribution will be made at the default rate applied against the amount of paid parental leave a person is receiving. National believes strong families are the cornerstone of a more prosperous society, and that starts with supporting every family to save for their future and build their own financial security.

4

### Employer Contributions for Workers Over 65

From 1 July 2027, National will require employers to pay the compulsory employer contribution for contributing KiwiSaver members aged over 65, on the same basis as for all other employees, from 1 July 2027.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Why is National making KiwiSaver compulsory?

National believes New Zealand is best served by shifting KiwiSaver to a compulsory savings model, where everyone is guaranteed to be more financially prepared for retirement, whether they work part-time, are self-employed, or just need a nudge to save a little more today in preparation for tomorrow.

### When will KiwiSaver contributions become compulsory?

National will make contributions to KiwiSaver (or an equivalent scheme) compulsory for all workers from 1 July 2028. Contributions will be made at the prevailing default rate as part of the agreed glidepath, lifting combined default contributions to 12% by 2032, matching Australia.

### Will self-employed people have to contribute?

Self-employed individuals would only be required to contribute the equivalent of the employee contribution. This means someone who is self-employed from 1 July 2028 will be required to contribute 4% of their income to their KiwiSaver (not the combined rate of 8%).

### How does the Baby Boost work?

Enrolment in KiwiSaver at birth will be automatic, and matched with a $1,500 Baby Boost payment to kickstart retirement savings, which will benefit from decades of compounding returns. For example, a $1,500 investment at birth, growing at a long-run average return of approximately 7% per annum, will be worth around $5,000 by age 18, even if there were no further contributions made in that time.

### What changes for over-65s?

From 1 July 2027, employers must pay the compulsory employer contribution for contributing KiwiSaver members aged over 65, ending the effective pay cut older workers currently face at 65.

## Enhancing KiwiSaver for Everyone
