# More medicines and earlier care

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/policies/more-medicines-and-earlier-care> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## More medicines and earlier care

Putting the health of Kiwis at home ahead of money sent overseas, delivering more medicines and earlier screening with no new taxes

Over this term, National has reduced wasteful spending to invest in the frontline, putting patients back at the heart of the health system with faster access to care and the largest ever funding boost for new cancer and other life-saving medicines. Now, National will lock in that progress and go further.

Responsible fiscal management is paying a dividend. Together, National and hardworking Kiwis have put New Zealand back on a path to surplus, and National will maintain that discipline by bringing money back home. We will reduce foreign aid outside the Pacific, where we will continue to support our closest neighbours and strongest interests. Every dollar saved will be put to work for Kiwis fighting cancer and other serious illnesses, with no new taxes.

A re-elected National Government will deliver a further $604 million uplift in Pharmac’s medicines budget, paid for by these savings. The last time National made this investment, it delivered 66 new medicines benefiting hundreds of thousands of Kiwis, including 33 new cancer treatments.

National will also back new ways to bring the latest treatments to New Zealand through more clinical trials and locally produced CAR-T cell therapy. Money that was once spent offshore will instead be invested in cutting-edge care, ensuring more Kiwis benefit from world-class treatment here at home.

## What we'll do

1

### Deliver a further $604 million uplift in Pharmac’s medicines budget

building on National’s track record of expanding access to new cancer and other life-saving medicines

2

### Turn responsible fiscal management into more medicines

by reducing foreign aid outside the Pacific

3

### Set a national target for clinical trials

in New Zealand, so more Kiwis can access the newest treatments sooner, with a focus on cancer and rare disorders

4

### Unlock CAR-T cell therapy

by supporting New Zealand’s medical sector to develop and produce this life-changing cancer treatment here at home

5

### Lower the free bowel screening age to 50 by 2029

backed by additional colonoscopies, so bowel cancer is caught earlier when it is most treatable

6

### Complete the free breast screening extension to age 74 by 2029

finishing the job National has started so more women have access to early detection

7

### Launch new screening pilots for prostate and lung cancer

so more cancers are found earlier

8

### Deliver free cervical screening for all women aged 25 to 69

from March 2027, so cervical cancer can be stopped before it starts

9

### Establish the Healthy Kiwis Programme

expanding active prescriptions with a target to double the number of people receiving them by 2030, helping more Kiwis get active, stay healthy, and avoid chronic diseases like diabetes.

## Building the Future: National's Economic Plan

To ensure hardworking New Zealanders can keep more of what they earn, get ahead, and build a more secure future.

Kiwis are among the hardest workers in the world, but we don't make as much for every hour worked as other countries. Over the last 40 years New Zealand has developed a productivity problem. National is fixing it.

Our Economic Plan means more jobs and higher wages. It means more money coming into local communities. It means we can afford more doctors, nurses, teachers, and better schools and hospitals.

We are making good progress. New Zealand is now growing faster than the US, the UK, Canada, Australia and Japan. Exports are up $20 billion, inflation is down from a 32-year high, interest rates have fallen, and 220,000 new jobs are forecast by 2030 with wages growing faster than inflation.

But there’s a lot more to do. If we stick to the plan that’s working, we can to build a future where hard work is rewarded and Kiwis can get ahead.

## National’s Economic Plan at a glance:

1

### Responsibly managing the books: a surplus in 2028/29 and debt below 40% of GDP over time

2

### Cutting red tape and supporting innovation: replacing the RMA and ending the war on farmers

3

### Delivering world-class education: an hour a day of reading, writing and maths, replacing NCEA, and more trades training

4

### Building infrastructure for the future: roads, hospitals, classrooms and energy.

# National’s plan to secure New Zealand’s future

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/policies/nationals-fiscal-plan> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## National’s plan to secure New Zealand’s future

New Zealanders have worked hard through a tough few years. National’s plan is about rewarding that hard work, letting more of what people earn stay in their pockets, and building a more secure future for families and businesses.

Maintaining a strong set of government books matters for New Zealanders. It is essential to delivering lasting prosperity for New Zealand and is one of the most practical things a government can do for household budgets.

Spending restraint helps take pressure off inflation and keep taxes low. When government debt is at moderate levels, interest rates are lower, the cost of financing this debt is less, and New Zealand has fiscal headroom when the next earthquake, severe weather event or global economic shock hits us.

When National entered government in 2023, we inherited a very difficult set of books, with ongoing budget deficits. Over the previous six years, government spending had gone up 70 per cent, and government debt had tripled. The interest costs on this debt were rising fast, and today taxpayers are still paying the equivalent of four Dunedin Hospitals every year just to cover them.

National introduced much-needed fiscal discipline. We did so by carefully prioritising where taxpayers’ money is spent, stopping spending in low-value areas and reinvesting it in the frontline services New Zealanders rely on such as hospitals and schools. In total, we have reprioritised around $50 billion over three Budgets to invest in frontline services, rather than increasing taxes to find the revenue.

As a result of our careful economic management, independent Treasury forecasts show that overall government spending is coming down as a proportion of the economy, a return to surplus is expected soon, and after next year the government debt curve bends down rather than up. Under a National Government, this fiscal repair will continue.

## What we'll do

1

### Not impose new taxes

2

### Continue investing in health, schools, law and order, roads, defence capability and other frontline services New Zealanders rely on

3

### Reprioritise spending and show ongoing restraint so that overall government expenditure comes down towards 30 per cent of GDP

4

### Return to surplus in 2028/29 and stay there

5

### Keep government debt on a downward trajectory towards 40 per cent of GDP and maintain debt below 40 per cent of GDP over time.

# Modernising Paid Parental Leave

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/policies/paid-parental-leave> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## Modernising Paid Parental Leave

Giving more support to mums and dads during one of the most important times of their lives

At the heart of National's plan to build the future are dedicated mums and dads, balancing long hours at work with the excitement and pressure that comes with raising young kids. The arrival of a new baby is often one of the happiest times in a family's life, but it also comes with higher costs and tough choices.

Now, National is laying out a long-term vision to modernise Paid Parental Leave as a whole and provide new mums and dads with the financial flexibility they need to spend more time at home with their new baby.

## Our Plan for Kiwi Families

### Extend paid parental leave

From 26 to 30 weeks in three stages over the next term, the first step in National's longer-term vision to extend paid parental leave to 40 weeks.

### Shared parental leave

Allow parents the flexibility to take their paid parental leave entitlement at the same time, or in overlapping instalments.

### Protect full holiday pay for new parents

Pass and protect new employment leave legislation so working mums and dads earn annual leave while on parental leave and are paid in full when they take it.

### KiwiSaver top-up

Government KiwiSaver contribution for people on paid parental leave, even if the person is not contributing themselves.

## Our Plan to Deliver

1

From 1 July 2027

Budget 2027

### 27 weeks

Paid parental leave entitlement increases from 26 to 27 weeks. Shared parental leave, full holiday pay protections for parents returning from parental leave, and KiwiSaver contributions on paid parental leave take effect.

2

From 1 July 2028

Budget 2028

### 28 weeks

Paid parental leave increases by a further week to 28 weeks.

3

From 1 July 2029

Budget 2029

### 30 weeks

Paid parental leave increases by two weeks to 30 weeks, four more weeks than today.

## More about the Policy

National is laying out a long-term vision to extend paid parental leave from six months to nine months, with an initial increase of four weeks over the next term.

Paid parental leave entitlements will increase from 26 weeks to 30 weeks over three Budgets — one week in 2027, one week in 2028, and two weeks in 2029.

Under National's policy, parents would have the option to take all or some of their paid parental leave at the same time.

New parents could mix and match their combined right to 30 weeks of paid parental leave as they see fit — together, then apart, then together again, in whatever order and combination works best for them. Every family has different needs.

Under the new Employment Leave Act, workers will continue to earn annual leave while on parental leave, and when they take annual leave after returning to work, they will be paid in full.

These changes take effect from 1 July 2027, ahead of the wider reforms, so parents see the benefit as soon as possible. A re-elected National Government will protect that legislation and oppose any efforts to water down the rights of working mums and dads.

National believes strong families are the cornerstone of a more prosperous society, and that starts with supporting every family to save for their future and build their own financial security.

From 1 July 2027, the Government will provide a KiwiSaver contribution to people on paid parental leave even if the person is not contributing themselves. The contribution is made at the default rate applied against the amount of paid parental leave a person is receiving.

# Keeping rates affordable

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/policies/rates-capping> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## Keeping rates affordable

So families can keep more money in their pockets, with rates increases that are more affordable and predictable

New Zealanders deserve stability and certainty when it comes to rates increases. Rates bills have been rising faster than many households can afford, with some communities experiencing double-digit increases year after year. We are committed to keeping rates affordable, refocusing councils on delivering core services, and ensuring more money stays in Kiwi pockets.

The Rates Capping Bill, which has now passed its first reading in Parliament, will help put an end to excessive and unexpected rates increases by requiring councils to keep annual rates increases within a target range of 2-4%. This approach balances the need for councils to continue delivering essential services while providing ratepayers with greater certainty and protection from unaffordable rates rises.

The Bill includes a minimum level of rates increase to support councils to continue delivering essential services and investing in infrastructure. It provides exemptions in exceptional circumstances where additional rates revenue is needed to recover from events such as natural disasters or where councils can demonstrate prudent financial management. However, councils will be required to consult their communities. At the same time, National will set up an independent regulator which will monitor compliance, assess exemption applications, and advise on future target ranges.

National believes that nice-to-haves should never come at the expense of delivering the basics and the days of double-digit yearly rates increases are coming to an end under a re-elected National Government.

## What we'll do

### Keep annual rates increases within the target range of 2 to 4%

### Implement the legislation in 2029 to save you money on your rates bill

### Establish an independent regulator to monitor compliance with the rates capping system

### Support councils through implementation and transition.

documents/policy-remove-rights-to-silenc.text:
# National to remove right to silence when a child is murdered

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/policies/remove-rights-to-silence> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## National to remove right to silence when a child is murdered

National is committed to fixing the basics in law and order, and building a future where all New Zealanders can feel safe in their communities.

A re-elected National Government will make it a crime to remain silent and not disclose information relating to a child being murdered.

New Zealanders will remember numerous high-profile examples throughout our history where children have been brutally murdered, and Police have been unable to identify the attacker because people have chosen not to share critical information with them.

The right to remain silent is a fundamental principle, however, it should not be absolute when a child has lost their life and, for example, there are only three people in the house, but no one is talking.

If re-elected, National will make it an offence under the Crimes Act to not disclose information to the police, when a person has been present at a location where a child 12 years and under has been killed. We will work with legal experts to create an exception to the general right to silence only in exceptional circumstances, involving the death of a child.

It will carry a maximum sentence of 10 years in prison. It will apply when a child under 12 dies, and at the time of death, or leading up to the death, it is unequivocal that one or more adults were present.

National is committed to fixing the basics in law and order, and building a future where all New Zealanders can feel safe in their communities. It is a basic expectation that people speak up and provide police with the information they need when investigating the death of a child.

Too many children in New Zealand die at the hands of, or with the knowledge of, people who should be protecting them. The right to silence should not be abused to the extent that these horrific crimes go unpunished.

This will place perpetrators, and their accomplices, into a corner where they will eventually call each other out, because if they don’t, they will all face the consequences.

# National's Budget Responsibility Rules

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/policies/responsibility-rules> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## National's Budget Responsibility Rules

To protect the economy so Kiwis can have more opportunities, higher wages and quality public services

A re-elected National Government will maintain three Budget Responsibility Rules to keep debt down, get back to surplus, and keep taxes low. These rules will provide the responsible economic and fiscal management needed to strengthen New Zealand’s financial resilience and enable greater investment in frontline services, like health, education, and law and order.

## What we'll do

1

### Prioritise a return to surplus in 2028/29 and maintain a surplus over time, sufficient to see the debt curve bend down

2

### Keep government debt on a downward trajectory towards 40 per cent of GDP and maintain debt below 40 per cent of GDP over time

3

### Keep taxes low by right-sizing government, with core Crown expenditure as a share of the economy declining towards 30 per cent of GDP

4

### Prioritise spending restraint and ongoing fiscal discipline rather than introducing new taxes on hard-working New Zealanders

5

### Support additional expenditure for frontline services through ongoing reprioritisation and reductions in lower-priority expenditure

6

### Continue investing in the roads, hospitals, schools and defence capability New Zealand needs, while ensuring investments deliver value for money and are consistent with responsible debt management.

## National's Budget Responsibility Rules

# National’s plan for retirement

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/policies/retirement> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## National’s plan for retirement

We will help seniors enjoy a more secure and independent retirement

Seniors have spent a lifetime contributing to New Zealand, and they deserve the security, respect, and opportunities to enjoy the retirement they have earned.

From Monday 26 October, Kiwi seniors will be able to vote on New Zealand’s future.

National is committed to recognising all that our older generations have given to this country and supporting them in retirement and into their old age. As a society, we must ensure you feel included and valued to live with dignity, respect and the security you deserve.

This election, there is a clear choice between sticking with National’s plan for a more secure future, no matter the stage of your life, with a growing economy, less debt, more jobs and higher wages.

Or going back to Labour – propped up by the Greens, Te Pāti Māori and TOP – who will undo the progress New Zealand has made over the last three years, leaving you to pay for it through at least nine new taxes costing households $2,263 each year.

Many retirees have spent a lifetime paying off their homes or have bought a rental property to top up their Super to support them in retirement. Now, these investments are at risk with TOP’s proposed Land Tax – and Labour’s own Capital Gains Tax.

The Land Tax would mean that if you have $500,000 worth of land in an urban centre, you will owe $8,750 a year in extra tax, on top of your rates bill.

And Labour’s Capital Gains Tax means an extra 28 per cent could be taken off investments that have built your retirement security.

There is no new money being proposed for seniors to help offset these costs, leaving you thousands of dollars worse off.

It’s unfair, and National won’t let it happen. Don’t put it all at risk.

By sticking to National’s plan, we will deliver a better future for retirees. A future where your finances are protected. A future where we invest responsibly in health, so you have peace of mind knowing you’ll get the care you need when you need it.

## What we'll do

1

### Establish a dedicated pipeline of affordable housing for seniors by ringfencing at least 20 per cent of places to seniors housing from the Housing Flexible Fund.

2

### Expand our successful granny flats policy so more can be built, faster, and cheaper.

3

### Make it easier to build tiny homes by expanding the granny flat rules to them, too.

4

### Establish 0800 Seniors a single free helpline to help seniors navigate government services and access the support they are entitled to.

5

### Strengthen protections against elder abuse and financial exploitation by reviewing the Enduring Powers of Attorney framework and considering further measures including law changes to better protect seniors from economic harm.

6

### Extend compulsory employer KiwiSaver contributions to contributing members aged over 65 from 1 July 2027 ensuring those who choose to keep working receive the same employer contributions as everyone else.

7

### Introduce no new taxes, protecting the savings seniors have worked a lifetime to build.

# Securing water and fertiliser to back NZ farmers

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/policies/securing-water-and-fertiliser> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## Securing water and fertiliser to back NZ farmers

National backs farmers as part of our plan to grow the economy, spend sensibly and get debt down, with no new taxes.

Reliable access to water and fertiliser is critical to on-farm productivity. National will remove roadblocks to new water storage infrastructure and reduce our exposure to volatile global fertiliser markets.

New Zealand’s farmers and growers are the best in the world. When they do well, the whole country does well. The primary sector produces 82 per cent of New Zealand’s exports and that money pays for the hospitals, schools and roads every community relies on. When farming grows, wages lift and our towns grow with it.

In much the same way as New Zealand ensures we have security of fuel and energy, security of water and fertiliser enables our farmers to produce food and generate the exports that are currently worth $65.2 billion to New Zealand’s economy.

When farmers and growers have reliable water, they produce more, take on more staff and more money flows into the local town, which means more jobs in regional communities.

National have an ambitious agenda for growth and the world wants what we produce. In three years, we have signed trade deals with India and the United Arab Emirates and completed an agreement with the Gulf states, and brought our deal with the European Union into force early. The job now is to produce more of it.

National back our farmers to get on with what they do best.

## What we'll do

1

### Commit $300 million in concessional loans to get water storage projects built

2

### The Primary Sector Growth Fund will continue to provide grants for feasibility studies

3

### Deliver New Zealand’s first long-term water infrastructure pipeline in partnership with farmers, growers, councils and iwi

4

### Publish the first National Rural and Provincial Water Use Strategy in 2027 backed by a national water storage register

5

### Introduce a National Standard for on-farm and other lower-risk off-stream water storage

6

### Introduce a National Standard for Irrigation to make consenting easier for farmers and growers

7

### Negotiate fertiliser security agreements with key supplier countries, using the New Zealand–Singapore Agreement on Trade in Essential Supplies as a model

8

### Establish a $10 million Critical Agri Inputs Fund to co-invest in fertiliser production, processing, storage and distribution projects from the Primary Sector Growth Fund.

# Home Energy Fund

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/policies/solar> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## Home Energy Fund

To lower your power bills and secure New Zealand’s energy future

National is focused on helping Kiwis become more energy independent and reduce their power bills by supporting them to electrify their own homes, farms, and small businesses. To make it easier for households and businesses to generate their own electricity, shops will be able to sell plug-in solar panels off the shelf within the first six months of a re-elected National Government.

A re-elected National Government will continue our plan to Electrify NZ by launching the Home Energy Fund, a central government and council-backed financing platform offering long-term loans for energy resilience investments, and by enabling electrification in the new planning system through clear national rules for small-scale renewables.

## What we'll do

### Launch the Home Energy Fund

A central government and council-backed financing platform offering long-term loans, secured against the home and repaid through rates, so households can invest in solar, batteries, insulation and other energy resilience measures without large upfront costs.

### Enable electrification in the new planning system

Set clear, national rules so that small-scale renewables, including rooftop and ground-mounted solar, micro-hydro and battery storage, are largely permitted as of right on your own property.

### Let property owners install rooftop solar without a consent

Allow rooftop solar without a consent, even where height limits or landscape overlays would otherwise get in the way.

### Make small-scale on-farm solar a permitted activity

Make small-scale on-farm ground-mounted solar a permitted activity with standard rules to manage genuine effects and sensible safeguards to protect land that is environmentally significant.

## Frequently Asked Questions

The Home Energy Fund is a national financing platform jointly owned by central government and participating councils that offers ratepayers low-interest, long-term loans secured against their property. The Home Energy Fund pays the approved installer upfront, and the homeowner repays the low-interest loan over ten years, either through a charge on their rates bill or on sale of their property.

Energy resilience investments eligible for support through the Home Energy Fund include residential solar and battery storage, insulation, heat pumps, and other investments in residential electrification.

Loans from the Home Energy Fund will be available to ratepayers with at least 20% equity in their property. The Home Energy Fund is jointly owned by central government and participating councils.

Kiwi families are under pressure from rising power bills. Rooftop solar, batteries, insulation and modern electric appliances can ease that pressure and make homes more resilient, but high upfront cost put them out of reach for many households, and existing green loans from commercial banks are limited. A re-elected National Government will implement the Home Energy Fund, a national financing platform jointly owned by central government and participating councils that offers ratepayers low-interest, long-term loans secured against their property.

We will set clear, national rules so that small-scale renewables – rooftop and ground-mounted solar, micro-hydro and battery storage – are largely permitted as of right on your own property.

Kiwis still face costly, confusing rules to develop small-scale renewables on their own property, making the process slow and expensive. There are huge opportunities to supercharge small-scale renewables like solar and micro-hydro on Kiwis’ own land. New Zealanders should be able to draw on the abundant natural resources on their own property with as little red tape as possible.

## Our Plan to Electrify NZ

# Tougher Sentences for Sexual Offending

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/policies/tougher-sentences> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## Tougher Sentences for Sexual Offending

Tougher Sentences for Sexual Offending

National will continue to ensure there are real consequences for crime by abolishing good character assessments at sentencing for all sexual offending. National is fixing the basics in law and order and building a future where all New Zealanders can feel safe in their communities. Ensuring there are real consequences for crime is a critical part of that.

## What we'll do

1

### Abolishing good character assessments at sentencing for all sexual offending

judges will be prohibited from treating good character as a mitigating factor at sentencing for all sexual offending.

2

### Tougher sentences

stopping judges from being forced to consider the public reputation of an offender when sentences for sexual offending are being handed down.

This builds on our previous work to limit the discounts judges can apply at sentencing to 40 per cent, giving sexual violence victims the power to determine whether their perpetrators receive permanent name suppression, and making stalking illegal and a jailable offence.

A vote for National is a vote for real consequences for crime.

# Making Trans-Tasman travel seamless

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/policies/trans-tasman-travel> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## Making Trans-Tasman travel seamless

By making it easier for Australians to visit New Zealand and explore our cities and regions.

Growing New Zealand’s tourism industry is a critical part of National’s plan to fix the basics and build the future. Tourism is our second-largest export earner and supports around one in nine jobs.

To support our shared tourism industry to keep growing, a re-elected National Government will work with Australia to trial seamless travel for Australian and New Zealand citizens travelling between the two countries. Making it easier for Australians to visit New Zealand means more visitors exploring our cities and regions which results in more incomes for local businesses, more job opportunities for New Zealanders, and a stronger economy.

National has already put the foundations in place for seamless travel. In 2009, the National-led Government officially launched SmartGate for trans-Tasman passengers. This was the first step in streamlining travel between the two countries.

## How it would work

1

### Eligible travellers (Australian and New Zealand passport holders) will provide their passport and travel details digitally before departure, building on information already provided to airlines and through the New Zealand Traveller Declaration.

2

### Complete their New Zealand Traveller Declaration before flying, allowing immigration, customs and biosecurity information to be assessed earlier.

3

### Have their eligibility and identity checked digitally, with travellers requiring further examination removed from the streamlined pathway.

4

### Use a dedicated trans-Tasman arrival pathway at Auckland, Wellington, Christchurch and Queenstown airports, which are supported by existing eGate and facial-recognition technology.

5

### Continue to meet all New Zealand biosecurity and customs requirements, including baggage inspection where required. Seamless immigration processing does not mean bypassing biosecurity. Travellers would still have to make the same declarations and could still have baggage inspected or be referred to an officer.

# A firm, fair and affordable welfare system

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/policies/walfare> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## A firm, fair and affordable welfare system

National believes those who can work should work. Employment is the best way out of hardship, giving people more independence, choices and opportunities.

New Zealand needs a welfare system that is firm, fair and affordable. It should provide a safety net when people need it, support Kiwis to move back into employment, and remain affordable for taxpayers. The longer someone remains on welfare, the harder it can become to return to work, with consequences for individuals, families and taxpayers.

However, under Labour, the number of people receiving a Jobseeker unemployment benefit for more than two years surged by 60 per cent – from 49,000 to 78,000 – between 2017 and 2023, despite unemployment falling over that period. Too many New Zealanders became stuck on welfare for years, rather than getting the support and facing the clear expectations needed to move back into work.

Since coming into Government, National has put employment back at the centre of the welfare system, restoring the principle of rights and responsibilities through clearer expectations and consequences under the Traffic Light System.

But there is more to do.

A re-elected National Government will build on the progress already made by investing earlier to help people move into work, while strengthening expectations for those who remain on Jobseeker long term. With Treasury forecasting 220,000 more people in employment over the next four years, we want to ensure Kiwis are ready to take up those opportunities, particularly in growth areas such as primary industries, construction and infrastructure, tourism and hospitality.

## What we'll do

1

### Investing earlier to help long-term Jobseekers into work

National will provide more intensive, work focused support for 30,000 work-ready jobseekers who have been on a benefit for more than a year, supporting them move into employment before long-term dependency becomes entrenched, with greater funding for employment programmes that support young people into work

2

### Stronger expectations after two years

From 1 April 2028, jobseekers who have received Jobseeker for two of the previous three years will move to a lower rate of payment, with a smaller reduction for households with dependent children

3

### Introduce random drug testing for Jobseekers

National will introduce random drug testing as part of MSD’s work-readiness and employment planning, starting with 10,000 tests in the first year and expanding the programme once established. Those who fail a second test will be required to undertake an alcohol and drug assessment, with continued non-compliance resulting in sanctions

4

### Double the stand-down for repeated voluntary unemployment

People who repeatedly leave employment without good and sufficient reason will face a 26-week non-entitlement period, up from 13 weeks

5

### Extending the benefit residency requirement to five years

From 1 April 2028, the minimum residence period for main benefits will increase from two years to five years.

# National’s plan to welcome more Kiwis home

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/policies/welcome-kiwis-home> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## National’s plan to welcome more Kiwis home

National will legislate and direct five key commitments in its first 100 days aimed at encouraging young New Zealanders to stay or return home to build their future.

A re-elected National Government will legislate and direct five key commitments in its first 100 days aimed at encouraging young New Zealanders to stay or return home to build their future, Finance and Economic Growth spokesperson Nicola Willis says.

National wants to make New Zealand the most attractive place for our young people to raise a family, build a career, start a business, and make a contribution to our country.

If re-elected, National will legislate and direct five key commitments in our first 100 days to make New Zealand more attractive and affordable for young people to live and work.

## These five commitments are:

1

### Lowering student loan repayment rates

for Kiwis living in New Zealand so they have more take-home pay when they need it most

2

### Widening access to 5 per cent deposits for first home buyers

so more people can overcome the barrier of the standard 20 per cent deposit

3

### Extending paid parental leave from 26 weeks to 30 weeks

within three years so that parents have more financial security while caring for their baby

4

### Strengthening KiwiSaver

including a $1500 Baby Boost payment and changes to contributions for parents on paid parental leave, so people can build bigger savings nest eggs to ensure greater financial security

5

### Prioritising and expediting work and visitor visas for partners of New Zealand citizens

so Kiwis who meet their partners overseas can bring them home when they return.

Each commitment has been fully funded to commence by 1 July 2027 in National’s fiscal plan (some may be earlier). Where a legislative change is needed to implement a commitment, National will pass the legislation in its first 100 days.

National has also committed to no new taxes, because helping hardworking Kiwis keep more of what they earn is a key part of our proposition for young people.

That is also why in 2024 we delivered income tax relief, giving average households with children an extra $78 a fortnight, and why we have been focused on keeping costs down by controlling spending to reduce debt and ease pressure on inflation and interest rates.

New Zealand’s lack of a capital gains tax is a real competitive advantage over Australia, and we should embrace that by not introducing one.

We want Kiwis living overseas to be excited about the opportunities New Zealand presents for them to get ahead and build a more secure future. Delivering those opportunities means growing the economy with things like new trade deals, a world-class education system and modern, reliable infrastructure.

We have made a lot of progress. We are growing faster than the US, the UK, Canada, and Australia. Exports are up $20 billion, inflation is down from a 32-year high, and 220,000 new jobs are expected with wages growing faster than prices.

It is encouraging to see more Kiwis returning home, with a 14 per cent increase in Kiwis moving back to New Zealand from Australia last year. But there is more to do and that means sticking with National’s plan which is working.

The alternative is a Labour Government propped up by the Greens, Te Pati Māori and Opportunity, planning nine new taxes and more of the same mistakes Labour made last time that forced Kiwis to leave in the first place.

If young New Zealanders want a more secure future, they should stick with the plan and party vote National.

# National’s plan for young adults

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/policies/young-adults> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## National’s plan for young adults

Our plan for young adults, we’ll deliver a future where you have the best opportunity to get ahead in life

From Monday 26 October, Kiwis will be able to vote on New Zealand’s future. National has a plan to help you secure your future, whether you’re a Kiwi kid, a young person starting out, a parent raising your family, or in your retirement.

This election, there is a clear choice between sticking with National’s plan for a more secure future, no matter the stage of your life, with a growing economy, less debt, more jobs and higher wages.

Or going back to Labour – propped up by the Greens, Te Pati Māori and TOP – who will undo the progress New Zealand has made over the past three years, leaving you to pay for it through at least nine new taxes costing households $2,263 each year.

Under our plan for young adults, we’ll deliver a future where you have the best opportunity to get ahead in life without having to move abroad. A future with a stronger economy, meaning more jobs and higher wages. A future where it is easier to pay off a student loan and buy your first home. A future where you get the services you rely on – all with no new taxes.

## What we'll do

1

### Lower student loan repayments

National will reduce the student loan repayment rate for Kiwis living in the country, leaving graduates with more take-home pay. This gives young people more income for rent, savings, a first home deposit or starting a business.

2

### Wider access to 5 per cent home loan deposits

National will expand access to the First Home Loan Scheme so more eligible buyers can purchase with a 5% deposit, rather than the conventional 20%.

3

### Paid Parental Leave extension

National is extending paid parental leave from 26-30 weeks to give parents more time with their newborn.

4

### Stronger KiwiSaver and $1500 Baby Boost

KiwiSaver will become compulsory, contribution settings will be higher, and a $1500 Baby Boost contribution will be made for each eligible newborn.

5

### A welfare system focused on work

Provide more intensive employment support for long-term jobseekers, alongside stronger expectations.

6

### No new taxes

Give workers, households and businesses greater certainty.

# National promises to fund $800 million Christchurch Northern Motorway extension

Source: <https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/politics_election-2026/1737541/national-promises-to-fund-800-million-christchurch-northern-motorway-extension> (RNZ (news report, third-party)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## National promises to fund $800 million Christchurch Northern Motorway extension

RNZ Parliamentary reporters

Caption: Christopher Luxon and other National Party candidates campaign in October 2026. Photo credit: Nathan McKinnon / RNZ

National is promising to fully fund an extension to the Christchurch Northern Motorway at the cost of $800 million in next year's budget, if it leads the next government.

National's transport spokesperson Chris Bishop said funding it in the next government's first Budget means construction can begin next year.

The party said it would fully fund the Belfast to Pegasus Motorway and Woodend Bypass, "the next major transport project Canterbury needs", said Bishop as he made the announcement in Christchurch.

"Canterbury is the engine room of the South Island... North Canterbury is one of the places where that growth is being felt most strongly."

Bishop said the Belfast to Pegasus Motorway and Woodend Bypass would extend the Christchurch Northern Motorway around 11 kilometres north, from just south of the Waimakariri River to beyond Pegasus and Ravenswood.

"SH1 approaching Woodend already carries around 21,500 vehicles a day, around nine percent of them freight, and that is expected to increase to around 28,000 vehicles a day by 2048."

He said that pressure was being felt in Woodend itself and at peak times it can take up to 20 minutes to travel through the town, while heavy through-traffic makes it harder for locals to access shops, schools and other parts of the community.

"There is also a significant safety problem. Between 2014 and 2023 there were 280 crashes on SH1 through Woodend, including three fatalities and 25 serious injuries.

"The new motorway and bypass will fundamentally change how this corridor works."

He said the project included widening the southern section of SH1 from two to four lanes, a new four-lane motorway bypass to the north, major intersection upgrades and new bridges.

NZTA estimated the project will save motorists up to 10 minutes at peak times, reduce traffic through Woodend from around 21,500 vehicles a day to 8000, and reduce deaths and serious injuries by 78 percent, Bishop added.

It would also make the corridor more reliable for people and freight travelling to and from Christchurch, Christchurch Airport and Lyttelton Port he said.

It wasn't a project "starting from scratch".

"Because of National's work in government, the project is ready to go and is the next investment-ready project on the Major Transport Projects Pipeline."

The announcement comes after National also promised to start construction on south Auckland's Mill Road if it leads the next government.

It would allocate $1.75 billion in Budget 2028 so construction can begin in late 2028, and look to progress route protection on Stages Two and Three by allocating $100m.

The Mill Road highway has been dogged in controversy for nearly two decades with political flip-flopping about building it, legal battles launched by climate advocacy groups and nearly 300 property owners left in uncertainty.

# Our Plan

Source: <https://www.national.org.nz/plan> (New Zealand National Party (national.org.nz)). Main article/policy content only; site navigation, footer and 'More policies/Latest news' lists removed. Text is verbatim.

## Full text

## Our Plan

By sticking to National's plan there will be a more secure future for all New Zealanders.

Economy

No New Taxes

Law & Order

Education & Health

When National came into Government two and a half years ago, Labour had left the country in deep trouble. The future did not look bright for Kiwis. The economy was damaged – inflation was at a 32-year high, mortgage repayments had skyrocketed, wages had stagnated, there were hundreds of ram raids a year, violent crime was rising, there was greater welfare dependency and children’s achievement was plummeting.

National has a long-term plan to turn that around. We’re making careful choices to create jobs and lift wages, say no to new taxes, stay tough on crime, and deliver the education and health services you deserve.

## National is fixing the basics and building the future by:

Growing the economy

## 1. Grow the economy to create jobs and boost wages.

2.7%
